Traveling back in time isn't simple, as James Cole (Bruce Willis) learns the hard way. Imprisoned in the 2030s, James is recruited for a mission that will send him back to the 1990s. Once there, he's supposed to gather information about a nascent plague that's about to exterminate the vast majority of the world's population. But, aside from the manic Jeffrey (Brad Pitt), he gets little in the way of cooperation, not least from medical gatekeepers like Dr. Kathryn Railly (Madeleine Stowe).
data.title: 12 Donkeys

data.description: Borat Sagdiyev, Kazakhstan's most oblivious journalist, is unleashed on the United States to make a documentary about “the greatest country in the world.” Armed with a broken English phrasebook, misplaced confidence, and a faulty moral compass, he collides with Southern hospitality, feminist meetings, rodeos, and Pamela Anderson, turning culture clash into a chaotic road trip that skewers prejudice and media gullibility.
data.title: Borat

data.description: Ex-Army Ranger Cameron Poe just wants to get home to his wife and daughter, but the transport plane carrying him and a gallery of lethal convicts is hijacked midair. With a DEA agent pushing to shoot the aircraft down and a rogue mastermind steering it toward the Las Vegas Strip, Poe teams up with a quick-thinking U.S. Marshal to outwit the criminals, protect the innocent, and land the flying powder keg safely.
data.title: Con Air

data.description: Disillusioned office drone Jack meets charismatic soap salesman Tyler Durden and is drawn into an underground fight club that becomes a violent therapy session for the modern male ego. As the club mutates into Project Mayhem—an anarchic movement bent on erasing consumer debt—Jack's grip on reality frays, forcing him to confront an alter ego that threatens the woman he loves and the world he helps destroy.
data.title: Fight Club

data.description: When astronomers discover a comet on a collision course with Earth, governments scramble to build an ambitious spacecraft that could split the rock before it triggers global extinction. As world leaders plan lotteries for underground shelters, veteran astronaut Spurgeon Tanner leads a crew of rookies into deep space, while a young reporter uncovers the political compromises, personal sacrifices, and quiet heroism hidden beneath the countdown to impact.
data.title: Deep Impact

data.description: Cynical TV weatherman Phil Connors is stranded in Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania, and wakes to the same Groundhog Day on repeat. Trapped in a time loop, he cycles through arrogance, indulgence, despair, and reinvention, using endless chances to learn piano, master small kindnesses, and earn the trust of producer Rita. Only when he embraces empathy and purpose does tomorrow finally arrive.
data.title: Groundhog Day

data.description: Overachieving London cop Nicholas Angel is exiled to the sleepy village of Sandford, where crime is supposedly limited to lost swans and rogue shoplifters. Partnered with affable movie geek Danny Butterman, he uncovers a secretive Neighborhood Watch masking a murderous conspiracy to keep the town “best village” perfect. As bodies pile up, the duo fight back with action-movie flair and a very British arsenal of garden tools.
data.title: Hot Fuzz

data.description: Leonard Shelby suffers from short-term memory loss after a brutal attack that killed his wife. He relies on Polaroids, handwritten notes, and tattoos to record clues while he hunts the man he believes responsible. Told in intersecting forward and reverse timelines, Leonard's investigation folds back on itself, revealing how fragile memory, revenge, and self-deception can be when the truth is written on skin.
data.title: Memento

data.description: In 2020, a seemingly routine Mars mission ends in catastrophe, leaving a lone survivor and a cryptic sand formation on the red planet. NASA assembles a rescue team led by veteran commander Woody Blake and systems specialist Jim McConnell, who recently lost his wife. As the crew confronts storms, dwindling fuel, and an alien signal carved into the Martian face, they must decide whether first contact is worth their lives.
data.title: Mission To Mars

data.description: In the post-Judgment Day wasteland of 2018, John Connor fights as a soldier rather than a savior, suspicious of mysterious drifter Marcus Wright, a death-row inmate revived with hidden cybernetics. As Skynet prepares to activate a new model that targets Connor and his father, the resistance must infiltrate the AI's fortress, rescue captured fighters, and decide whether machines can earn a second chance at humanity.
data.title: Terminator Salvation

data.description: Average Joe Bauers is selected for a military hibernation experiment and forgotten for five centuries. He awakens in a future where corporate slogans replace science, crops are watered with sports drinks, and intelligence has nosedived. Mistaken for a genius, Joe teams with former prostitute Rita to fix the failing ecosystem and outwit a proudly dim president, discovering that common sense is now the most precious resource.
data.title: Idiocracy

data.description: In Los Angeles, hitmen Vincent Vega and Jules Winnfield debate morality between assignments for crime boss Marsellus Wallace, whose wife Mia shares a dangerous night out with Vincent. A past-his-prime boxer double-crosses Marsellus, a pair of diner thieves pick the wrong breakfast spot, and a glowing briefcase ties the threads together. Dark humor and circular storytelling turn pulp cliches into a pop-culture mosaic about chance and consequence.
data.title: Pulp Fiction

data.description: Cuban refugee Tony Montana claws his way from dishwasher to Miami cocaine kingpin, fueled by paranoia, limitless ambition, and a mountain of powder. As his empire expands through ruthless violence and flashy excess, Tony's world narrows to a fortress guarded by loyal friend Manny and icy wife Elvira. Betrayal, federal pressure, and his own rage push him toward a bloody last stand beneath the neon glow of the American dream.
data.title: Scarface

data.description: Small-time boxing promoter Turkish and his partner Tommy tangle with a stolen diamond, a temperamental crime boss named Brick Top, and an underground boxing match that keeps changing rules. When they recruit bare-knuckle brawler Mickey O'Neil, every plan collapses into chaos involving inept crooks, snarling dogs, and untrustworthy getaway drivers. The London underworld collides in a kinetic, darkly comic scramble for survival and profit.
data.title: Snatch

data.description: When Ba'al steals the Stargate and rewrites history, SG-1 members find themselves in an altered Earth where the program never existed. Racing against a collapsing timeline, Mitchell, Carter, Jackson, and Teal'c hijack a time-traveling ship to stop Ba'al at the moment he changed the past. They must restore the original timeline, rescue stranded teammates, and decide whether the price of victory is their own erasure.
data.title: Stargate: Continuum

data.description: On his first day with the elite LAPD narcotics unit, rookie Jake Hoyt rides with decorated detective Alonzo Harris and plunges into a whirlwind of raids, shakedowns, and moral compromises. As hours pass, Jake realizes Alonzo's charismatic swagger masks corruption and a deadly debt to ruthless gangsters. With the clock ticking toward midnight, Jake must choose between loyalty to his badge and survival on streets Alonzo claims to own.
data.title: Training Day

data.description: After three years in prison for killing neo-Nazis who attacked his family, Derek Vinyard tries to pull his younger brother Danny away from the white-supremacist gang he once led. Flashbacks reveal how rage and propaganda radicalized him, while the present forces Derek to confront old allies, mend shattered family trust, and decide whether redemption can overpower the cycle of hate he set in motion.
data.title: American History X

data.description: Sixties superspy Austin Powers is thawed in the 1990s to stop bald archvillain Dr. Evil from holding the world ransom. Armed with crushed-velvet suits, dubious dental work, and unlimited “mojo,” Austin fumbles through culture shock, seduction, and spycraft alongside agent Vanessa Kensington, proving that shagadelic confidence sometimes beats high-tech espionage when global catastrophe is on the line.
data.title: Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery

data.description: In Qing dynasty China, legendary sword Green Destiny is stolen, pulling stoic warrior Li Mu Bai and disciplined Yu Shu Lien into pursuit. They clash with headstrong aristocrat Jen, who secretly yearns for freedom and wields lethal skill. Across deserts, bamboo forests, and moonlit rooftops, honor, duty, and forbidden love collide as each must choose between tradition and the lives their hearts demand.
data.title: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon

data.description: Broke single mother Erin Brockovich stumbles onto medical records linking a California town's cancers to a utility's tainted groundwater. Lacking legal training but armed with grit, charm, and outrage, she wins the trust of sick families, wrangles a skeptical law firm, and builds a massive class-action case that proves everyday tenacity can shake a corporation and deliver justice to ordinary people.
data.title: Erin Brockovich

data.description: Journalist Raoul Duke and his lawyer Dr. Gonzo roar toward Las Vegas with a trunk of narcotics, chasing a story that dissolves into kaleidoscopic hallucinations. Through casino floors, desert highways, and motel paranoia, they skewer the American Dream, exposing how excess, advertising, and fear warp a nation already halfway to madness.
data.title: Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas

data.description: Analyst-turned-agent Maxwell Smart finally gets his field assignment when spy agency CONTROL is compromised. Paired with ultra-competent Agent 99, he bumbles through ballroom brawls, gadget mishaps, and a bomb plot by KAOS. His eagerness and oddball instincts prove unexpectedly useful as the duo race to stop nuclear sabotage and show that enthusiasm can fill the gaps where training fails.
data.title: Get Smart

data.description: German industrialist Oskar Schindler arrives in Nazi-occupied Poland seeking profit and status, but the brutality against Jews transforms his factory into a refuge. By risking fortune, reputation, and ultimately his life, he shields over a thousand workers from extermination, proving one pragmatic opportunist can tilt history through courage and conscience.
data.title: Schindler's List

data.description: FBI profiler Will Graham, scarred from catching Hannibal Lecter, is pulled back to hunt the Tooth Fairy, a killer who stalks families by moonlight. Graham must rekindle his dangerous empathy for monsters, trading insights with Lecter while racing to decode the next victim's fate, knowing that each step deeper threatens his sanity and the people he's sworn to save.
data.title: Red Dragon

data.description: Solitary hitman Leon lives by strict rules until 12-year-old Mathilda, whose family is murdered by a corrupt DEA agent, begs for sanctuary. As he trains her in his lethal craft, their surrogate bond challenges his detachment and her innocence, pushing both toward a confrontation where loyalty and vengeance collide in a New York apartment siege.
data.title: Leon: The Professional

data.description: After a crooked card game leaves four London friends owing half a million pounds to a brutal crime boss, their scramble for cash entangles them with a pair of antique shotguns, drug growers next door, and humorously inept thugs. Misheard plans and razor timing send every party colliding in a chaotic shootout where luck is as valuable as aim.
data.title: Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels

data.description: Across one stormy day in the San Fernando Valley, a dying game-show host, a guilt-ridden cop, a drug-addled quiz-kid grown up, and wounded families intersect. As frogs fall from the sky and secrets erupt, they search for forgiveness and connection, suggesting that coincidence may be grace in disguise even when life feels impossibly heavy.
data.title: Magnolia

data.description: Orphaned billionaire Bruce Wayne trains with the League of Shadows, then returns to Gotham to become Batman, waging war on mobster Falcone and fear-wielding psychiatrist Scarecrow. With allies Alfred, Rachel, and Jim Gordon, he embraces symbol over flesh, turning terror back on criminals while uncovering a larger plan to burn the city he swore to save.
data.title: Batman Begins

data.description: Haunted profiler Will Graham, still scarred from capturing Hannibal Lecter, is lured out of retirement to stop the Tooth Fairy, a killer fixated on family slaughter. Graham's empathy lets him mirror the murderer, but that gift risks his sanity, especially as Lecter toys with him from behind bars and the next full moon approaches.
data.title: Manhunter

data.description: In 2054 Washington, D.C., Precrime police arrest killers before they act, guided by visions from three precogs. When chief John Anderton appears in a vision murdering a stranger, he flees his own system, uncovering political motives and the moral cost of trading freedom for safety.
data.title: Minority Report

data.description: When her aging father is conscripted, fearless Fa Mulan disguises herself as a man and takes his place in the Chinese army. Guided by a disgraced dragon guardian and her own resolve, she masters combat, thwarts a Hun invasion, and challenges the limits of tradition to bring honor to her family and empire.
data.title: Mulan

data.description: Cubicle drone Peter Gibbons is hypnotized into not caring about his soul-crushing tech job, inspiring him and friends Michael and Samir to embezzle fractions of cents from their company. Office politics, a malfunctioning printer, and a flair-obsessed chain restaurant become battlegrounds in this anti-corporate satire.
data.title: Office Space

data.description: The cash-strapped Kim family infiltrates the lavish home of the wealthy Parks by posing as unrelated specialists. Their fragile scheme unravels when a hidden basement secret surfaces, igniting class tensions, dark humor, and a brutal scramble for survival that questions who is truly parasitic in a society built on inequality.
data.title: Parasite

data.description: From polar peaks to ocean trenches, this series captures animals as they hunt, migrate, court, and survive in rarely seen ways: snow leopards ambush Himalayan ibex, great white sharks rocket through seal colonies, desert elephants dig for hidden water. Majestic aerials and time-lapse sequences reveal how fragile these ecosystems are—and how quickly they're changing under human pressure.
data.title: Planet Earth

data.description: Filmed with lightweight 4K rigs, this sequel returns to frozen seas, coral reefs, and jungles to show behaviors never captured before: mobula rays leaping by moonlight, glass frogs guarding eggs, lizards surfing ocean currents. Each vignette pairs wonder with a quiet warning about bleaching reefs, plastic debris, and the narrow margins animals now navigate.
data.title: Blue Planet II

data.description: Narrated by David Attenborough and scientist Johan Rockström, this film visualizes the nine planetary boundaries—climate, biodiversity, oceans, freshwater—and shows how collapsing ice shelves, burning forests, and bleaching reefs signal tipping points. Hopeful case studies outline how rapid policy shifts could stabilize Earth's life-support systems still within reach.
data.title: Breaking Boundaries: The Science of Our Planet

data.description: Using ultra-slow motion and remote cameras, this series shows how animals time every move to daylight cycles: cheetahs pacing dawn hunts, bees reading ultraviolet patterns, nocturnal hyenas raiding under stars. Scientists explain circadian clocks, lunar rhythms, and how light pollution scrambles instincts, forcing wildlife to rewrite ancient schedules.
data.title: Earth at Night in Color

data.description: High-speed drones and motion-triggered rigs follow David Attenborough through seven continents, from Antarctic penguin crèches to Andean pumas and Australian bushfires. Each chapter pairs charismatic species with the specific human pressures they face—overfishing, mining, warming seas—arguing that protecting biomes is as urgent as protecting individual animals.
data.title: Seven Worlds, One Planet

data.description: Intimate jungle footage captures mountain gorilla families in Rwanda's Volcanoes National Park. The documentary traces their social hierarchy, gentle play, and fierce territorial battles while echoing Dian Fossey's conservation legacy. It highlights how ecotourism funds rangers who risk their lives against poachers to keep this recovering population alive.
data.title: Gorillas in the Mist: A Closer Look

data.description: Camera traps inside termite mounds, ant towers, and underground fungus farms reveal insect megacities built with cooling chimneys, farming chambers, and chemical alarm highways. Biologists decode how swarms make decisions without leaders and how their architectures inspire human design, while also warning how pesticides threaten these unseen engineers.
data.title: Insects: The Secret World

data.description: Using thermal cameras, aerial infrared, and ranger bodycams, this film follows anti-poaching units in Kenya and South Africa as they race to save elephants and rhinos targeted for ivory. Night ambushes, informant networks, and courtroom battles reveal a cat-and-mouse war where wildlife crime funds international cartels.
data.title: The Ivory Game

data.description: NASA, ESA, and NOAA scientists race to decode why coral reefs are bleaching at record rates. Underwater macro shots show symbiotic algae abandoning corals; drone surveys map reefs turning ghostly white. Local fishers, Pacific islanders, and marine biologists weigh what losing reefs means for food, storms, and culture.
data.title: Chasing Coral

data.description: Aerial cinematography and time-lapse photography sweep across 25 countries to show Earth without narration—deserts, swamps, megacities, and farms—inviting viewers to sense patterns of water, light, and human footprint. The visual poem underscores interdependence between natural cycles and civilization's relentless expansion.
data.title: Samsara

data.description: From blistering dunes to kelp forests, this feature shows how predators and prey sharpen each other: cheetahs sprinting after impala, great white sharks breaching for seals, wild dogs coordinating hunts. Slow motion and predator-mounted cams reveal strategy and sensory finesse while stressing how habitat loss disrupts these finely tuned rivalries.
data.title: Nature's Great Events: Predators

data.description: Life inside oceans explodes in close-up: dolphins corralling sardines with bubble nets, cuttlefish flashing camouflage, and coconut octopuses using shells as armor. Filmed with rebreathers and gyro-stabilized cameras, the documentary reveals how currents, coral nurseries, and predator hierarchies knit together the planet's richest biome.
data.title: Oceans

data.description: From California forests to Tibetan plateaus, filmmaker Louie Schwartzberg shows how fungi connect trees, recycle life, and may unlock new medicines. Microscopic time-lapses make spores bloom like fireworks while mycologists explain networks rivaling the internet. The film blends wonder with a plea to protect soils underpinning every ecosystem.
data.title: Fantastic Fungi

data.description: High in China's Qinling mountains, camera crews follow giant panda mothers raising cubs through snow and bamboo scarcity. Biologists detail how fragmented forests and low birth rates endanger the species, while captive-breeding breakthroughs and rewilding experiments hint at a fragile comeback for the planet's most famous bear.
data.title: Pandas: The Journey Home

data.description: Following nomads across the Arctic Circle, the film records caribou migrations, musk ox standoffs, and polar bears teaching cubs to hunt seals on thinning ice. Indigenous hunters describe how sea-ice calendars shift, reshaping food security and culture. The stark footage underscores how fast the North is warming.
data.title: Wild Arctic

data.description: Slow-motion cinematography dives into a honeybee colony: queen rearing, waggle dances, comb engineering, and battles with hornets. Researchers explain how pesticides, mites, and habitat loss drive colony collapse, while urban beekeepers and farmers test remedies from wildflower corridors to genome tracking.
data.title: The Secret Life of Bees

data.description: Macro and thermal lenses shrink viewers to the scale of a backyard. Ant wars, hummingbird heartbeats, fox kits under a shed, and raccoons solving garbage puzzles reveal urban ecosystems thriving beside humans. Ecologists show how light, noise, and food waste reshape behavior, turning cities into evolving wildlife laboratories.
data.title: The Wild in the City

data.description: Hidden-camera rigs in Brazil's Pantanal track jaguars fishing, giant otters patrolling lagoons, and hyacinth macaws rebuilding nests. Conservationists partner with ranchers to protect cattle and cats simultaneously, proving that predator coexistence hinges on corridors, compensation, and community pride in the world's largest tropical wetland.
data.title: Jaguars: Brazil's Super Cats

data.description: Africa's great rivers—the Congo, Nile, and Zambezi—are explored from source to delta. Drone shots and underwater rigs reveal tigerfish launching out of water, hippos carving channels, and shoebill storks ambushing lungfish. Communities along the banks describe floods, hydropower plans, and how shifting rains reshape both wildlife and livelihoods.
data.title: Rivers of Life: Africa

data.description: When Steven Avery is exonerated by DNA after 18 years in prison, he sues local law enforcement—then is charged with a new murder. Over two seasons, filmmakers track trials, appeals, and media fallout, questioning coerced confessions, evidence handling, and how poverty shapes a defendant's odds. The series asks if the system corrects errors or compounds them.
data.title: Making a Murderer

data.description: Reclusive real-estate heir Robert Durst is linked to three killings across decades. Through interviews, archival evidence, and Durst's mic'd asides, filmmaker Andrew Jarecki reconstructs missing wives, dismembered roommates, and a confession-capping finale that stunned viewers and prosecutors alike.
data.title: The Jinx: The Life and Deaths of Robert Durst

data.description: After novelist Michael Peterson's wife is found dead at the bottom of their staircase, a French crew films his trial for 16 years. From blood-spatter debates to a surprise owl theory, the series shows how experts, jurors, and family fracture under the weight of reasonable doubt and narrative spin.
data.title: The Staircase

data.description: The first of three films on the West Memphis Three traces how three Arkansas teens were convicted of child murders amid satanic-panic fervor. Courtroom footage, metal-band T-shirts, and inconsistent confessions reveal a rush to judgment that later evidence and appeals would dismantle.
data.title: Paradise Lost: The Child Murders at Robin Hood Hills

data.description: Picking up the West Memphis Three story with new DNA tests and celebrity-backed appeals, this film chronicles Damien Echols' fight from death row. Investigators revisit witnesses, jurors question their verdicts, and the Alford plea looms—showing how public pressure and science can pry open a case but not erase trauma.
data.title: West of Memphis

data.description: A missing French teenager seems to resurface in Texas as a dark-eyed Spaniard who convinces family and officials he is their son. Interviews and reenactments peel back layers of lies, asking why grieving relatives accept an obvious imposter and how truth warps when hope collides with bureaucracy.
data.title: The Imposter

data.description: Errol Morris reopens a 1976 Texas murder case against drifter Randall Dale Adams. Stylized reenactments, shifting witness stories, and a hypnotic Philip Glass score expose shaky police work and prosecutorial tunnel vision, ultimately helping overturn Adams' conviction and reshaping documentary crime storytelling.
data.title: The Thin Blue Line

data.description: Surveillance tapes, chat logs, and interviews reveal how internet sleuths hunt a killer who posted cat torture videos online. Their digital trail crosses borders, escalating as the culprit graduates to murder, raising uneasy questions about vigilantism, viral cruelty, and the internet's role in manufacturing criminals and detectives alike.
data.title: Don't F**k with Cats: Hunting an Internet Killer

data.description: Football star Aaron Hernandez is convicted of murder while hiding CTE, sexuality conflicts, and gang ties. The series weaves trial audio, prison calls, and neurologists' findings to explore how brain trauma, identity, and celebrity intersect in a fall from NFL glory to life without parole.
data.title: Killer Inside: The Mind of Aaron Hernandez

data.description: Baltimore high-school classmates investigate the 1969 murder of Sister Cathy Cesnik, uncovering allegations of priest abuse and a church coverup. Interviews with survivors, former students, and detectives reveal how institutional power can bury truth for decades until grassroots persistence forces it into daylight.
data.title: The Keepers

data.description: Through police interviews and court footage, Amanda Knox recounts her Italian murder trial, media frenzy, and years of appeals. Journalists and prosecutors defend their narratives, illustrating how tabloids, cultural bias, and prosecutorial pride can eclipse evidence in the scramble to assign guilt.
data.title: Amanda Knox

data.description: Interrogation experts revisit cases where suspects confessed, only for later evidence to cast doubt. Tapes show long, coercive interviews; psychologists explain false memories; families push for exonerations. The series questions whether confession-centric policing produces truth or expedient closures that imprison the innocent.
data.title: The Confession Tapes

data.description: Interviews, police files, and first responders' accounts chart the hunt for Richard Ramirez, the “Night Stalker,” who terrorized 1980s California with home-invasion murders. Detectives detail stakeouts, media leaks, and shoe-print evidence, while survivors describe living with trauma long after an arrest ended the spree.
data.title: Night Stalker: The Hunt for a Serial Killer

data.description: Survivors, jurors, and detectives recount the 1989 Central Park jogger case, showing how five Black and Latino teens were coerced into confessions, convicted, and later exonerated by DNA and a true perpetrator's admission. The film indicts media hysteria, racial bias, and the fragility of justice for marginalized youth.
data.title: The Central Park Five

data.description: Each episode follows a real exoneration from crime to conviction to release, blending forensic re-analysis, lab scandals, and eyewitness fallibility. Lawyers from the Innocence Project detail how junk science and mistaken IDs seep into verdicts, while freed clients navigate life after decades lost.
data.title: The Innocence Files

data.description: A 1984 Oregon cult led by Bhagwan Shree Rajneesh builds a desert city and clashes with locals, triggering bioterror attacks, mass poisoning, and an assassination plot. Through archival footage and insider interviews, the series examines how utopian dreams curdled into paranoia and how power struggles tore the commune apart.
data.title: Wild Wild Country

data.description: When a Colorado mother and her two daughters vanish, police bodycams, neighbor videos, and text messages unravel the facade of a perfect family. Investigators chart Chris Watts' shifting stories until forensic evidence and failed polygraphs force a confession, exposing the banality and brutality of familicide in suburbia.
data.title: American Murder: The Family Next Door

data.description: A Utah family befriends a charismatic neighbor who kidnaps their daughter twice, manipulating parents and exploiting religious trust. Interviews, FBI testimony, and archived TV appearances reveal how grooming, gaslighting, and community silence let a predator operate in plain sight.
data.title: Abducted in Plain Sight

data.description: This epic series traces human history from the big bang to the 21st century, using CGI timelines, dramatizations, and expert narration. Episodes link the rise of empires, trade routes, plagues, revolutions, and scientific breakthroughs, showing how climate shifts, resources, and ideas repeatedly reshaped societies and set the stage for our interconnected world.
data.title: Mankind: The Story of All of Us

data.description: Peter Jackson restores WWI footage from Britain's Imperial War Museum, colorizing frames and syncing soldier interviews to immerse viewers in trench life. Lice, mud, camaraderie, and shellfire replace silent newsreel distance, reminding modern audiences of the youth, humor, and terror behind century-old faces.
data.title: They Shall Not Grow Old

data.description: From gold-thirsty conquistadors to independence struggles, this series charts Latin America's past, weaving archival art, letters, and reenactments. It shows how indigenous resistance, slavery, religion, and resource extraction forged nations—and how those forces still echo in modern politics, borders, and identity.
data.title: Conquest of the Americas

data.description: A four-part series on the Dust Bowl uncovers how mechanized plowing, drought, and speculation turned America's plains into a black blizzard zone. Diaries, black-and-white film, and survivor voices convey suffocating storms, mass migration, and New Deal soil programs that reinvented farming practices to heal the land.
data.title: The Dust Bowl

data.description: Through declassified memos and survivor testimony, this film reconstructs the 1986 Chernobyl meltdown: control-room errors, delayed evacuations, and the heroism of firefighters and divers who stemmed radioactive lava. It examines Soviet secrecy, the Exclusion Zone's lasting scars, and how nuclear policy shifted worldwide after the plume crossed continents.
data.title: Chernobyl: Inside the Disaster

data.description: Animated maps, letters, and veteran voices recount D-Day from both Allied and German perspectives. Paratroopers dropping into hedgerows, beachhead chaos, and the race to secure Caen show how weather gambles, deception plans, and raw logistics determined the largest amphibious invasion in history.
data.title: D-Day: The Untold Stories

data.description: Drawing on diaries and battle footage, this film follows the Harlem Hellfighters—an all-Black regiment in WWI—through training, trench combat, and jazz tours in France. It contrasts valor with the racism they faced at home, tracing how their service fueled civil-rights momentum and changed American music.
data.title: The Harlem Hellfighters

data.description: Archaeologists, laser scans, and archival footage unearth Pompeii moments before Vesuvius erupted: bakeries mid-loaf, gladiator barracks, painted taverns. The film pieces together escape routes, toxic gases, and ash flows to reconstruct the last day, while showing how modern digs and 3D mapping rewrite what we know about Roman daily life.
data.title: Pompeii: Secrets of the Dead

data.description: Eyewitnesses and newly released tapes revisit the fall of the Berlin Wall: East German protests, Stasi files burned in basements, and a botched press conference that opened the border. The documentary shows how ordinary citizens, miscommunications, and geopolitical fatigue ended a divided city overnight and reshaped Europe.
data.title: 1989: The Fall of the Berlin Wall

data.description: Through letters, plantation ledgers, and freedpeople's testimonies, this film traces the transatlantic slave trade's economic engine and human toll. It follows ships from West African coasts to Caribbean auctions and American cotton fields, then tracks how abolitionist networks, revolts, and the Civil War dismantled legal slavery—leaving legacies still visible today.
data.title: Slavery and the Making of America

data.description: Framed by diaries and battlefield sketches, this series recounts the American Civil War: secession debates, ironclads on the Mississippi, Emancipation Proclamation politics, and Sherman's march. Scholars and re-enactors explore how industrial logistics, telegraph lines, and photography made it the first modern war.
data.title: Civil War 360

data.description: The story of the Apollo program's Saturn V rocket: Cold War urgency, von Braun's engineering gambles, and assembly inside NASA's VAB. Engineers recount F-1 engine failures, lunar-module docking trials, and the nerve-wracking countdown of Apollo 8—culminating in humanity's first view of Earthrise from lunar orbit.
data.title: Moon Machines: Saturn V

data.description: Recovered archives and survivor interviews recount the 1994 Rwandan genocide: radio broadcasts inciting violence, UN hesitation, and neighbors turning on neighbors. The film follows rescue corridors, hotel refuges, and post-genocide gacaca courts, asking how a nation confronts memory while rebuilding institutions and trust.
data.title: Ghosts of Rwanda

data.description: Tracing the Wright brothers from Dayton bicycle shop to Kitty Hawk's dunes, historians unpack wind-tunnel tests, stall crashes, patent fights, and how war contracts shaped early flight. Restored photos and replica flights show how their three-axis control system became the blueprint for every modern aircraft.
data.title: The Wright Brothers: First in Flight

data.description: Set against Shanghai's neon boom, this documentary examines how modern China was carved by Opium Wars, civil strife, Japanese invasion, and Communist revolution. Economists and historians track how treaty ports, railways, and state planning forged today's superpower while leaving contested memories in textbooks and public squares.
data.title: China: A Century of Revolution

data.description: Newly declassified cables and cockpit audio recount the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis: U-2 flights photographing silos, backchannel letters between Kennedy and Khrushchev, and a Soviet sub nearly launching a nuclear torpedo. The hour-by-hour narrative shows how misread intentions nearly triggered war and how restraint averted it.
data.title: The Cuban Missile Crisis: Three Men at the Brink

data.description: Rare colorized reels show the 1947 partition of British India into India and Pakistan: last-ditch negotiations, trains filled with refugees, and violence as borders slice through Punjab and Bengal. Survivors recall lost homes and divided families; diplomats reflect on how hurried cartography sowed decades of conflict.
data.title: The Partition of India

data.description: Archaeologists and radar scans peel back layers of Angkor Wat, revealing hydraulic canals, hidden shrines, and why the Khmer Empire collapsed. Monsoon failures, political strife, and shifting trade routes are mapped across jungle temples, linking past resilience to present-day preservation battles in Cambodia.
data.title: Angkor Wat: Secrets of the Empire

data.description: Street artists around the world wage a playful and political war with walls—stencils in Paris, guerrilla posters in LA, murals in Bethlehem. As anonymous prankster Banksy turns the camera on fellow vandal Thierry Guetta, the film morphs into a satire about authorship, hype, and how the art market can commodify rebellion overnight.
data.title: Exit Through the Gift Shop

data.description: Ruth Bader Ginsburg's path from Brooklyn prodigy to Supreme Court icon is told through case files, workouts, and family banter. Former clerks and rivals recount her strategy on gender equality, while memes and pop-culture nods show how an octogenarian justice became the “Notorious RBG,” bridging law and fandom.
data.title: RBG

data.description: In Oakland, filmmaker Boots Riley guides viewers through housing protests, tech displacement, and the legacy of the Black Panthers. Barbershop debates, BART rides, and street murals reveal a city wrestling with identity as rents soar and culture is repackaged for newcomers.
data.title: We Are the Town

data.description: Eight anonymous Tehran teens risk arrest to record their lives: underground raves, rooftop skate sessions, and private unveilings of hair and hijabs. Smuggled footage reveals a generation fluent in Instagram and satire, negotiating tradition, surveillance, and desire inside a city that never fully sleeps or surrenders.
data.title: Raving Iran

data.description: From ballroom halls to Bronx blocks, this film traces the roots of voguing and house culture. Elders explain chosen families, category battles, and why “shade” is language, armor, and art. Modern kiki scenes show how queer Black and Latinx youth still carve joy and safety on dancefloors despite gentrification and policing.
data.title: Paris Is Still Burning

data.description: A portrait of the global #MeToo wave, following survivors, lawyers, and reporters as they challenge power structures from Hollywood to Seoul. The film intercuts press briefings, labor-union rallies, and trauma therapy, asking how culture, law, and social media can or cannot deliver accountability for gendered abuse.
data.title: This Changes Everything

data.description: Filmed over 12 years, this documentary shadows an undocumented Mexican family in New York. Births, ICE raids, PTA meetings, and legalization hopes show how policy debates land on kitchen tables, and how children move between American dreams and deportation fears.
data.title: The Second Motherland

data.description: Exploring K-pop's ascent, this film moves from Seoul training academies to stadium world tours. Trainees drill vocals and choreography 14 hours a day, negotiate contracts, and cultivate fandoms on social apps. Industry critics question mental health costs and cultural export ambitions behind the meticulously engineered sparkle.
data.title: Idol Factories: Inside K-Pop

data.description: How street food sustains cities: from Bangkok boat noodles to Mexico City tacos al pastor. Vendors share recipes, debts, and resilience while historians trace migration and spice routes that created these flavors. Mouthwatering close-ups pair with policy debates over permits, hygiene, and gentrification's squeeze on informal economies.
data.title: Street Food Nations

data.description: Black photographers, filmmakers, and musicians dissect how images of Blackness are framed, feared, or fetishized. From civil-rights newsreels to Instagram, they examine who holds the camera and why representation still shapes safety, opportunity, and self-definition in America.
data.title: Black Lens

data.description: An oral history of the modern internet told by the people who coded it: TCP/IP pioneers, browser builders, and protocol hackers. Whiteboard sketches, packet traces, and startup garage photos reveal how open standards triumphed, and how commercialization and surveillance now test the ethos of early net freedom.
data.title: The Web We Made

data.description: Following five high-school seniors in Chicago's South Side, the film tracks college apps, gun violence, part-time jobs, and prom nights. Teachers and parents fight to keep students on track as budget cuts and neighborhood pressures loom, illustrating how zip codes still script opportunity in America.
data.title: South Side Graduates

data.description: A cross-country ride on long-haul trucks reveals America's hidden highways: CB radio slang, warehouse waits, lot lizards, and 14-hour clocks. Drivers discuss deregulation, opioid pain, and rest-stop loneliness, while economists explain how every grocery shelf depends on a labor force few people ever see.
data.title: Rolling Country

data.description: Portraits of barbershops from Lagos to London show chairs as therapy couches and news desks. Haircuts become rituals of community, migration memory, and style politics. Shop talk debates sports, elections, and masculinity while historians trace how Black barbers once financed civil-rights organizing.
data.title: Cut/Style

data.description: Comedian Hasan Minhaj dissects the cost of weddings across diasporas: South Asian dowries, American Pinterest pressure, and destination inflation. Newlyweds and planners lay out budgets, spreadsheets, and cultural expectations, revealing how love ceremonies often become economic negotiations and social signaling exercises.
data.title: The Big Day Equation

data.description: With handheld cameras, activists live-stream the 2013 Brazilian bus fare protests as they swell into nationwide marches about corruption and inequality. Tweets, tear gas, and city-council votes intertwine, showing how smartphones turned citizens into broadcasters and reshaped public space and police response.
data.title: Uprising: Streams of Change

data.description: A day inside Lagos's Balogun Market follows traders bargaining in Yoruba, Igbo, and pidgin; porters hauling bales; and bankers on scooters collecting cash. Economists and sociologists unpack how informal economies power megacities, while sellers describe credit chains, border closures, and the pride of hustling in Africa's busiest bazaar.
data.title: Market Hustle: Lagos

data.description: Prince's studio tapes, purple tour footage, and bandmates' memories chart the restless genius who fused funk, rock, and gospel while fighting for artistic ownership. Engineers break down how he built songs alone at Paisley Park, while legal battles over masters show the cost of demanding freedom in a corporate industry.
data.title: Prince: Sign of the Times

data.description: Through letters, cockpit audio, and family interviews, the film follows Neil Armstrong from Navy test flights to commanding Apollo 11. Simulations, fatal training accidents, and the moon EVA reveal a stoic engineer balancing grief and fame, while post-mission years show his retreat to teaching and quiet advocacy for space safety.
data.title: Armstrong

data.description: Letters, photos, and FBI files trace Fred Rogers' ministry of kindness on public television. Colleagues describe how he tackled divorce, assassination, and race with puppets and songs, while cultural critics debate whether his soft-spoken ethos can withstand today's polarized media landscape.
data.title: Won't You Be My Neighbor?

data.description: Simone Biles recounts her path from foster care to gymnastics supremacy: 25 world medals, GOAT pressure, and her Tokyo decision to prioritize mental health. Coaches dissect Amanars and triple-doubles; teammates discuss abuse revelations that forced the sport to confront athlete safety and autonomy.
data.title: Simone: The Twisties and the Triumph

data.description: Nobel laureate Malala Yousafzai narrates her childhood in Pakistan's Swat Valley, the Taliban attack that nearly killed her, and her global education campaign. Classroom visits and UN speeches sit alongside quiet Oxford dorm moments, showing an activist balancing public expectations with private adulthood.
data.title: Malala: One Child, One Teacher

data.description: James Baldwin's unfinished manuscript anchors a journey through Black American history from Medgar Evers to Martin Luther King Jr. Samuel L. Jackson's narration overlays television archives and protests, linking past and present struggles against racism and asking what America would be without the people it has oppressed.
data.title: I Am Not Your Negro

data.description: Diego Maradona's Napoli years unfold through 500 hours of unseen footage: chaotic Serie A crowds, mafia entanglements, trophies, and late-night excess. Friends and foes recount how a slum kid carried a city's hopes, then crumbled under fame and addiction, redefining the price of soccer divinity.
data.title: Diego Maradona

data.description: From tequila bars to Coachella, “Despacito” producer Benny Blanco traces Latin pop's crossover boom. Shakira, J Balvin, and sound engineers break down beats, Spanglish hooks, and streaming algorithms that catapulted reggaeton worldwide, while critics note how representation and commerce mingle on the global charts.
data.title: Latin Fire: The Global Pop Wave

data.description: Gamer-turned-astronaut Chris Hadfield recounts how a Cold War childhood obsession led to commanding the ISS. Helmet cams show spacewalks, while his viral guitar videos and zero-G science demos reveal how social media rewrote astronaut outreach. The film balances awe with the minutiae of checklists, exercise, and orbital teamwork.
data.title: Space Oddity: Chris Hadfield

data.description: Tony Hawk narrates how backyard ramps birthed modern skateboarding. Archival VHS, X Games runs, and hospital bills chart pioneers like Rodney Mullen and Elissa Steamer pushing physics and gender norms. Industry insiders dissect sponsorship booms, video games, and how aging skaters manage bodies built on risk.
data.title: Bones and Boards: A Skate Story

data.description: “The White Helmets” follow Syrian volunteers who race into bombed buildings to pull survivors out. Helmet cams show dust-choked rescues, improvised gear, and moments of dark humor that keep despair at bay. As cities fall, the film questions how ordinary citizens bear responsibilities usually reserved for states.
data.title: The White Helmets

data.description: Chef Massimo Bottura risks his Modena restaurant's three Michelin stars by closing, reinventing classics, and launching food-waste soup kitchens. Kitchen crises, parmesan wheel avalanches, and philosophical debates about tradition vs. innovation reveal how art, activism, and cuisine intertwine.
data.title: Massimo: Theatre of Taste

data.description: With backstage passes and therapy sessions, Taylor Swift examines the construction of her public persona: country prodigy, pop titan, political latecomer. Songwriting voice memos, stadium rehearsals, and a battle over master recordings show a woman negotiating control of her art and image under relentless spotlight.
data.title: Miss Americana

data.description: Hidden-camera and courtroom footage follow Chinese billionaire Xu Jie as he fights pollution lawsuits against state-backed factories. His rise from rural poverty to outspoken tycoon reveals the collision of wealth, conscience, and censorship in a country sprinting toward modernization.
data.title: The Billionaire Rebel

data.description: Edward Snowden's life after the Hong Kong hotel: asylum in Moscow, encrypted calls with journalists, and his marriage lived under surveillance risk. Philosophers and cryptographers debate whistleblowing ethics while Snowden codes privacy tools, insisting that ordinary citizens deserve agency over their data.
data.title: Citizen Snowden

data.description: Serena Williams' final tour blends childcare, comeback training, and the decision to step away from tennis. Coaches analyze serve mechanics; rivals reflect on how she reshaped power play and prize equity. The film ends not with a match result but with her framing retirement as “evolution,” redefining legacy on her own terms.
data.title: Serena: Evolution

data.description: Four insurgent women—including bartender-turned-candidate Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez—challenge establishment Democrats in the 2018 primaries. Door-knocking marathons, debate prep, and bare-bones budgets contrast with slick incumbents, showing how grassroots frustration over healthcare and inequality can upend long-entrenched power.
data.title: Knock Down the House

data.description: Cambridge Analytica whistleblowers and data scientists reveal how harvested Facebook profiles, psychographic ads, and dark posts targeted voters in Brexit and the 2016 U.S. election. Lawsuits, hearings, and leaked decks expose a new propaganda battlefield, asking whether privacy and democracy can survive surveillance capitalism.
data.title: The Great Hack

data.description: Journalist Glenn Greenwald, filmmaker Laura Poitras, and NSA contractor Edward Snowden meet in a Hong Kong hotel to expose mass surveillance. Claustrophobic room scenes, encrypted uploads, and global headlines show how secrecy gives way to the most consequential leak of the digital age—and its personal cost for the leaker.
data.title: Citizenfour

data.description: Republican strategist Steve Schmidt and Obama aide Ben Rhodes revisit the 2008 and 2012 U.S. elections, unpacking messaging, money, and microtargeting that rewired campaigning. Field offices, voter files, and debate prep illustrate how data and narrative merged to decide turnout, setting templates both parties still emulate.
data.title: The Battle for the White House

data.description: Former U.S. Defense Secretary Robert McNamara delivers 11 lessons from Vietnam, WWII firebombing, and the Cuban Missile Crisis. Archive tapes and glass-wall interviews reveal a man grappling with remorse, statistics, and the foggy boundaries between rational policy and catastrophic moral failure.
data.title: The Fog of War

data.description: Michael Moore connects the Bush family, Saudi elites, and the post-9/11 War on Terror. Congressional walkouts, wounded soldiers, and Saudi evacuation flights are stitched together to question how fear, contractors, and media framing propelled the Iraq invasion and redefined American civil liberties.
data.title: Fahrenheit 9/11

data.description: Ava DuVernay revisits U.S. history from the 13th Amendment to mass incarceration, arguing that a loophole for “punishment for crime” enabled Black Codes, Jim Crow, and the War on Drugs. Scholars, activists, and politicians tie policy to profit, asking whether the carceral state is slavery by another name.
data.title: 13th

data.description: Inside campaign buses and policy huddles, this film follows three 2020 presidential campaigns as they court early states, chase small donors, and battle misinformation. Staffers debate whether authenticity or message discipline wins in a cycle shaped by pandemic upheaval and social movements demanding sweeping change.
data.title: Run for President

data.description: “The War Room” peers inside Bill Clinton's 1992 presidential run, trailing strategists James Carville and George Stephanopoulos as they spin scandals, wrangle debates, and invent rapid-response tactics. Smoke-filled headquarters become a laboratory for modern political messaging and the 24-hour news cycle we now take for granted.
data.title: The War Room

data.description: Climate activist Greta Thunberg sails across the Atlantic to address the UN, skipping flights to underscore emissions. Behind the podium clips, the film shows lonely train rides, panic attacks, and family debates, framing a teenager's rise into a symbol of global protest and the backlash she endures from powerful skeptics.
data.title: I Am Greta

data.description: Captured over five years, “Weiner” follows former congressman Anthony Weiner's failed 2013 New York mayoral bid as new sexting scandals erupt. Strategy meetings, shouting matches, and late-night apologies reveal how personal implosions derail campaigns and how tabloid spectacle consumes substantive policy debate.
data.title: Weiner

data.description: Using long-withheld audio from Richard Nixon's secret tapes, this film revisits Watergate: break-ins, hush money, Saturday Night Massacre firings. Journalists, aides, and historians chart how paranoia, loyalty tests, and an “enemies list” unraveled a presidency and cemented checks on executive power.
data.title: Watergate: Blueprint for a Scandal

data.description: Economists and policymakers unpack the 2008 financial crash: subprime mortgages, AIG swaps, and the decision to let Lehman fail. Whistleblowers chart how deregulation and ratings agencies fueled a bubble; laid-off workers show the human toll; reformers debate whether post-crisis rules can curb the next meltdown.
data.title: Inside Job Revisited

data.description: Following journalists from The Guardian and Washington Post, this film chronicles the Panama Papers leak: 11.5 million files exposing offshore shelters for politicians, athletes, and criminals. Reporters dodge legal threats and sift shell-company mazes, proving collaborative cross-border journalism can puncture secrecy regimes.
data.title: Panama Papers: Public Trust vs. Private Wealth

data.description: Afghan interpreters who aided U.S. troops race to secure visas as withdrawal looms. Interviews in Kabul safe houses and Washington corridors show bureaucratic limbo, Taliban threats, and advocates battling to honor promises. The film indicts how policy delays become life-or-death for allies left behind.
data.title: Promises in Translation

data.description: Following the 2013 Hong Kong protests, student leaders, lawyers, and shopkeepers debate autonomy under the “one country, two systems” promise. Umbrella-filled streets, tear gas, and courtroom battles reveal how civic identity collides with Beijing's tightening grip—and how ordinary citizens weigh protest against personal cost.
data.title: Umbrella City

data.description: Charts the rapid rise of right-wing populism across Europe: rallies in Hungary, Brexit bus tours, French yellow vests. Political scientists connect economic austerity, migration fears, and social media echo chambers, while activists and refugees rebut nationalist rhetoric on the ground.
data.title: Europe: The New Nationalists

data.description: Last Dance cameras trail the 1997-98 Chicago Bulls as Michael Jordan pushes for a sixth title amid front-office rifts. Locker-room clashes, Pippen's contract standoff, Rodman's Vegas detour, and Phil Jackson's triangle tweaks reveal how egos, fatigue, and legacy anxiety collide in a dynasty's final sprint.
data.title: The Last Dance

data.description: Filmed over five years, two Chicago teens chase basketball scholarships while navigating injuries, academics, and violence. Coaches, parents, and recruiters shape their futures, revealing how talent, zip code, and luck intertwine in America's unofficial farm system for the NBA.
data.title: Hoop Dreams

data.description: Formula One champion Ayrton Senna's career is told through cockpit radio, family archives, and on-track duels with Alain Prost. The film covers Monaco masterclasses, political battles with the FIA, and the fatal Imola crash, exploring how charisma and risk forged a legend who remains revered decades later.
data.title: Senna

data.description: Surfing prodigy Bethany Hamilton loses an arm to a shark at 13, then fights back to world tour form. Training montages, adaptive board rigs, and wipeouts show resilience; interviews explore faith, motherhood, and what it means to redefine strength when the ocean that injured you remains your greatest pull.
data.title: Bethany Hamilton: Unstoppable

data.description: Nine-part series on O.J. Simpson traces his football stardom, celebrity marriage, racial tightrope, and the murder trial that split America. Archival news, 911 calls, and juror reflections reveal how sport, fame, policing, and race collided into the “trial of the century.”
data.title: O.J.: Made in America

data.description: A cycling doping experiment leads filmmaker Bryan Fogel to Russian chemist Grigory Rodchenkov, who exposes state-sponsored cheating. Lab raids, whistleblower exile, and IOC fallout expand a personal test into a geopolitical sports scandal that reshaped global anti-doping rules.
data.title: Icarus

data.description: Behind-the-scenes of Conor McGregor's meteoric rise from Dublin welfare to UFC champion. Sparring-room clashes, press-conference theatrics, and the Mayweather payday reveal an athlete who weaponized swagger as business strategy, while coaches and family question how long body and brand can withstand perpetual combat.
data.title: Conor McGregor: Notorious

data.description: Iceland's underdog soccer team, drawn from tiny clubs and part-time dentists, shocks Europe at Euro 2016. Locker-room speeches, Viking clap crowds, and data-driven coaching show how a nation of 330,000 built belief and tactics to topple giants, redefining what resourceful teamwork can achieve.
data.title: Rise of the Vikings: Iceland's Miracle Team

data.description: ESPN's 30 for 30 chronicles Bo Jackson's two-sport brilliance: NFL power runs, MLB moonshot homers, and the hip injury that ended it all. Teammates and trainers reflect on raw athleticism, while Nike ad architects explain how “Bo Knows” built the modern cross-sport brand idol.
data.title: You Don't Know Bo

data.description: Formula One docuseries dives into team radios, engineering bays, and contract dramas. From Mercedes vs. Red Bull title fights to Haas budget woes, it shows how tire temps, wind tunnels, and ego management decide split-second outcomes and billion-dollar sponsorships.
data.title: Drive to Survive

data.description: After frostbite ends his NFL dream, Nate Boyer joins the Army, then walks on to Texas Longhorns football as a 30-year-old long snapper. The film follows midnight study halls, parachute jumps, and special-teams drills, exploring patriotism, grit, and what it means to chase impossible second chances.
data.title: The Long Snap

data.description: Running back A.C. Green's 1,192 consecutive NBA games become a study in durability and discipline. Trainers dissect recovery routines; teammates recall locker-room pranks; sports scientists compare his Iron Man streak to modern load management, asking whether today's stars could—or should—push bodies that far.
data.title: Iron Man: The A.C. Green Story

data.description: Tennis legends Borg and McEnroe relive their 1980 Wimbledon clash: icy baseline patience versus fiery serve-and-volley aggression. Match stats, wood-racket physics, and sports psychologists unpack how rivalry forged respect and raised the sport's mental bar.
data.title: Borg vs. McEnroe: Fire and Ice

data.description: Behind the roar of the Tour de France, this film follows domestiques hauling water, team cars plotting on radio, and soigneurs patching road rash. Power-meter data meets Alpine descents to show how teamwork and watts—not just solo heroics—decide yellow jerseys.
data.title: Peloton: Inside the Tour

data.description: Free climber Tommy Caldwell and partner Kevin Jorgeson attempt the Dawn Wall of Yosemite's El Capitan, spending weeks on the vertical face. Bloodied fingertips, portaledge nights, and phone calls to family capture how obsession, partnership, and meticulous planning conquer a route once deemed impossible.
data.title: The Dawn Wall

data.description: Cameras follow Kenyan marathoner Eliud Kipchoge's quest to break the two-hour barrier. Wind-tunnel testing of pacing formations, laser-guided splits, and bespoke shoes meet philosophical musings on discipline. The Vienna run shows how precision teamwork and one runner's calm reshaped what humans believe is possible.
data.title: 2:00:00 - Kipchoge's Impossible Run

data.description: Spit and sawdust to Olympic snow parks, “Art of Flight” follows snowboarders Travis Rice and friends chasing perfect lines worldwide. Helicopter drops, avalanches, and stomped tricks show equal parts artistry and risk, while Red Bull budgets and drone shots reveal how action sports became cinematic spectacle.
data.title: The Art of Flight

data.description: British Olympic diver Tom Daley prepares for Worlds while juggling YouTube fame, coming out, and marriage. Physios manage shoulder strains; sports psychologists steady nerves on 10-meter platforms. The film shows how identity, media, and precision technique intertwine when your career hangs on one splash.
data.title: Splash: Tom Daley's Edge

data.description: Former U.S. Vice President Al Gore travels city to city with a slide deck that turns melting glaciers, hurricane tracks, and CO₂ graphs into an urgent plea. Classroom anecdotes mix with bipartisan policy nudges, framing climate change not as distant science but as a solvable civic crisis if voters, businesses, and governments act in time.
data.title: An Inconvenient Truth

data.description: Photographer James Balog deploys time-lapse cameras on Greenland, Alaska, and Iceland ice fronts to witness glaciers racing backward. Shattering seracs, collapsing melt ponds, and multi-year sequences become visual proof of warming, while field teams battle broken tripods, frostbite, and crevasse fields to keep the record rolling.
data.title: Chasing Ice

data.description: Leonardo DiCaprio travels from sinking Pacific atolls to Alberta's tar sands, grilling ministers, oil CEOs, and climate scientists. Animated carbon budget charts and Papal interviews push viewers to weigh policy, diet, and energy choices, arguing that denial is no longer a political option as feedback loops accelerate.
data.title: Before the Flood

data.description: Ocean advocate Sylvia Earle reflects on half a century underwater—from pioneering submersibles to confronting mass fish decline and reef loss. Archival dives blend with modern expeditions to deep blue holes as she rallies “Hope Spots,” arguing that protecting 30 percent of the ocean is the minimum for planetary health.
data.title: Mission Blue

data.description: Former vegan-turned-investigator Kip Andersen follows the carbon and water math of beef and dairy, challenging big green NGOs on why they seldom confront livestock's footprint. Feedlots, rainforest clear-cuts, and methane statistics clash with personal diet choices, sparking debate over whether sustainability must go plant-based.
data.title: Cowspiracy: The Sustainability Secret

data.description: Seaspiracy traces how industrial fleets, bycatch, and subsidies ravage oceans. Undercover footage shows shark finning and plastic “ghost nets,” while whistleblowers say eco-labels fail at sea. The film argues personal straw bans are dwarfed by trawlers and urges viewers to reconsider seafood's hidden ecological price.
data.title: Seaspiracy

data.description: Filmmaker Damon Gameau visits researchers and farmers to model a future 2040 if today's solutions scale: regenerative agriculture storing carbon, seaweed farms feeding cattle to cut methane, microgrids powering villages, and transport swaps that shrink oil demand. Animated “what if” sequences turn policy whitepapers into hope-filled storyboards.

Gasland journeys across U.S. shale plays where fracking has brought royalties—and flaming tap water. Residents ignite kitchen sinks, doctors report mysterious illnesses, and companies deny contamination. Josh Fox weaves banjo solos with legal documents, questioning whether cheap gas justifies risks to aquifers and rural health.
data.title: Gasland

data.description: From feedlots to grocery aisles, “Food, Inc.” uncovers how a handful of corporations control meat and grain supplies. Hidden-camera slaughterhouses, corn subsidies, and patent-enforced seeds show a system optimized for efficiency but rife with obesity, migrant exploitation, and polluted rivers—urging consumers to wield forks like votes.
data.title: Food, Inc.

data.description: “Virunga” follows rangers in Congo's Virunga National Park as they shield mountain gorillas from poachers and an oil company's ambitions. Hidden cameras catch bribery attempts and militia threats, while the team fortifies bunkers and bottle-feeds orphaned apes—showing conservation as frontline war in a region rich in life and conflict.
data.title: Virunga

data.description: “Racing Extinction” rigs hybrid cars with projection systems to beam endangered species onto skyscrapers while tracking wildlife trafficking from Hong Kong markets to Amazon ranches. Undercover stings, methane-measuring cameras, and activist street art merge into a global call to halt a sixth mass extinction in motion.
data.title: Racing Extinction

data.description: Using bottle dives and microplastic trawls, “A Plastic Ocean” shows how discarded packaging breaks into toxic confetti eaten by fish and returned to human plates. Remote atolls piled with debris, seabirds starved by full bellies, and recycling economists reveal both the scale of the problem and circular-economy fixes already working.
data.title: A Plastic Ocean

data.description: “DamNation” tracks America's aging dams and the movement to tear them down. Kayakers, tribal leaders, and fisheries biologists celebrate salmon runs rebounding after removals like Elwha and Edwards. Archival propaganda of hydro triumphs sits beside drone shots of cracked spillways, asking when concrete shifts from progress to liability.
data.title: DamNation

data.description: “Kiss the Ground” digs into regenerative farming: cover crops, no-till drills, and mob-grazing cattle that rebuild soil carbon. Soil scientists, ranchers, and Woody Harrelson's narration argue that healthy dirt can reverse desertification and draw down gigatons of CO₂ while boosting yields and rural economies.
data.title: Kiss the Ground

data.description: Fashion's hidden costs unfold from Dhaka dye vats to Texas cotton fields. Workers explain poverty wages and factory fires; rivers run neon with runoff; consumers confront fast-fashion churn. The film connects closets to carbon, urging fair wages, slower cycles, and transparent supply chains as levers for systemic change.
data.title: The True Cost

data.description: “Arctic Tale” follows a polar bear cub and a walrus calf growing up on shrinking sea ice. Hunting lessons, playful slides, and first swims are shadowed by thinning floes and longer swims to food. Narration links their intimate struggles to the broader story of a warming Arctic reshaping cultures and food webs.
data.title: Arctic Tale

data.description: “RiverBlue” journeys from China to Bangladesh and the U.S., showing how denim and leather tanneries dump heavy metals and indigo into rivers. Paddleboard host Mark Angelo meets scientists testing toxic loads and designers pioneering waterless dye tech, arguing consumer choice and regulation can turn fashion from polluter to partner.
data.title: RiverBlue

data.description: From Hawaii to the Maldives, “Plastic Paradise” tracks how single-use plastics travel ocean gyres to remote beaches. Beach cleanups, polymer chemistry, and industry lobbyists collide as filmmaker Angela Sun dissects why recycling rates lag and what bans, refill systems, and citizen pressure can do to stem the tide.
data.title: Plastic Paradise: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch

data.description: TV series about the life of Brendon Small, an eight-year-old visionary who, using his friends Jason and Mellisa as actors, have managed to direct over a thousand homemade films. His parents are divorced, but it doesn't feel strange since so many other kids' parents are divorced. His friend Jason actually feels upset because his parents are still together. At school, he is taught soccer by his coach John McGirk, or as he calls him, "that weird Irish guy".
data.title: Home Movies
I Don't Do Well in Parent-Teacher Conferences
The Art of the Sucker Punch
It Was Supposed to Be Funny
Breaking Up is Hard to Do
Those Bitches Tried to Cheat Me

data.description: Charlie Babbitt expects a fortune from his late father and instead discovers he has an older autistic brother, Raymond, living in an institution. Desperate for money, Charlie kidnaps Ray for a cross-country trip to battle over inheritance, but card counting, roadside mishaps, and awkward motel nights force both men to confront family wounds, responsibility, and the unexpected connection they never knew they needed.
data.title: Rain Man

data.description: In Brighton Beach, four addicts chase different dreams—a TV game-show fantasy, a fashion model's diet, a small-time drug hustle, and a romantic future that keeps slipping away. Pills and powders warp their bodies and minds, turning ambition into hallucination. As debt, prison, and amputation loom, the film charts how hope curdles into delusion when every escape is chemical and every choice tightens the spiral.
data.title: Requiem for a Dream

data.description: Six criminals known only by color-coded aliases botch a diamond heist and regroup in a warehouse to stitch together what went wrong. Bleeding cops, missing loot, and clashing alibis spark paranoia that one of them is an undercover officer. Tarantino's debut mixes nonlinear interrogation, pop-culture banter, and sudden brutality into a pressure cooker where loyalty fractures and everyone weighs betrayal against survival.
data.title: Reservoir Dogs

data.description: Blind, retired lieutenant colonel Frank Slade hijacks a prep schooler's Thanksgiving break for one last lavish fling: five-star hotels, Ferraris on Manhattan streets, and a show-stopping tango. As the student faces an honor code dilemma back at school, Slade contemplates suicide unless loyalty, candor, and a fiery courtroom speech can restore his faith in himself and the young man he's unexpectedly mentoring.
data.title: Scent of a Woman

data.description: Shaolin monk Sing reunites his washed-up kung fu brothers and fuses ancient kicks with street soccer, forming a misfit team that hammers shots with chi-fueled bicycle kicks. As they face bribed referees and steroid-fueled rivals, slapstick set pieces and wire-fu mayhem turn the tournament into a spectacle where brotherhood and belief matter more than the trophy.
data.title: Shaolin Soccer

data.description: London slacker Shaun coasts through dead-end work and pub nights until a zombie outbreak forces him to rescue his mum, win back his girlfriend, and hole up at the Winchester bar. Cricket bats, LPs used as weapons, and gallows humor collide with genuine stakes, proving that friendship and quick thinking can keep you alive—even when your apocalypse plan is built around pints.
data.title: Shaun of the Dead

data.description: In Frank Miller's rain-slick Basin City, multiple revenge tales collide: Marv hunts the killers of a street angel, Dwight protects prostitutes from a crooked cop, and Hartigan saves a girl from a sadistic predator. Stark black-and-white panels turned into motion, splashes of color, and hardboiled narration create a lurid noir world where justice is carved with fists, blades, and bullets.
data.title: Sin City

data.description: When a terrorist rigs a Los Angeles bus to explode if speed drops below 50 mph, rookie cop Jack Traven and passenger Annie must keep the bus barreling through traffic, unfinished freeways, and police roadblocks. A cat-and-mouse game with the bomber turns a city commute into a relentless high-octane siege where split-second choices decide who gets off alive.
data.title: Speed

data.description: Baltimore rebel Tyler Gage vandalizes a school and is sentenced to mop floors at its elite arts conservatory. There he meets dancer Nora, whose senior showcase needs a partner. Tyler's street moves and Nora's classical technique fuse into something fresh, forcing both to choose between safe paths and a risky shot at reinvention, love, and escape from the lives that seemed prewritten.
data.title: Step Up

data.description: Navin Johnson cheerfully stumbles from rural sharecropper life to inventing a bizarre eyeglass grip that rockets him into sudden wealth. Fame brings gold-plated absurdities, lawsuits, and assassins, sending him back down the ladder in a string of slapstick misfortunes. Through banjos, dogs, and carnival romance, Navin stays convinced destiny owes him one more ridiculous turn.
data.title: The Jerk

data.description: In 2057, the sun is fading. A multinational crew aboard the Icarus II carries a stellar bomb to reignite it. As they near the star, equipment sabotage, oxygen shortfall, and a deranged survivor from the lost Icarus I force them into terrifying choices about who lives, who dies, and whether humanity's hope outweighs individual survival or sanity.
data.title: Sunshine

data.description: Andy Stitzer is a 40-year-old electronics clerk who never had sex and never cared—until well-meaning friends push him onto the dating circuit. After disastrous speed dates, chest-waxing, and cringe karaoke, he meets a single mom who actually sees him. The comedy digs beneath raunch to show how honesty and patience can trump bravado in a culture obsessed with experience over connection.
data.title: The 40-Year-Old Virgin

data.description: Bowling-obsessed slacker Jeffrey “The Dude” Lebowski seeks restitution after thugs soil his rug, mistakenly targeting him instead of a millionaire with the same name. His quest pulls in a kidnapped trophy wife, a severed toe, nihilist bowlers, and Vietnam flashbacks from best friend Walter. Amid White Russians and gutterballs, the Dude learns that chaos abides—and sometimes abiding is enough.
data.title: The Big Lebowski

data.description: Amnesiac assassin Jason Bourne races through Moscow, Madrid, London, Tangier, and New York evading CIA kill teams while hacking clues to his own creation in the black-ops program Treadstone. Rooftop chases, close-quarters fights, and a damning file reveal the price of weaponizing a man, pushing Bourne to expose the agency even if doing so paints a permanent target on his back.
data.title: The Bourne Ultimatum

data.description: Lonely customer Steven Kovacs orders cable service and gets Chip, an overzealous installer who decides they're best friends. Chip's boundary-smashing “gifts” include medieval restaurant brawls and staged arrests that derail Steven's relationships and career. Dark comedy turns stalkerish as Steven realizes escaping Chip's clingy grip may require broadcasting the truth of their toxic “friendship.”
data.title: The Cable Guy

data.description: FBI trainee Clarice Starling seeks the mind of imprisoned cannibal Hannibal Lecter to stop serial killer Buffalo Bill. As she trades personal truths for clues, time runs out for a kidnapped victim. Lecter's taunts, moth symbolism, and basement night-vision showdown create a psychological and procedural thriller about how monsters recognize each other across prison bars and mirrors.
data.title: The Silence of the Lambs

data.description: Escaped convict Riddick is recaptured by mercenaries, only to crash with them on planet Crematoria, where sunlit hours scorch flesh and night unleashes winged predators. Pursued by a fanatical Necromonger army bent on conquest, Riddick bargains with bounty hunters, old allies, and an air elemental to survive a triple threat of heat, darkness, and zealotry.
data.title: The Chronicles of Riddick

data.description: In 2263 New York, cabbie Korben Dallas collides with Leeloo, a perfect being who embodies a mysterious Fifth Element needed to stop a cosmic evil approaching Earth. With a manic TV host, a gun-running tycoon, and priests guarding ancient secrets, they race through floating traffic, opera houses, and alien temples to assemble four elemental stones before the universe's timer runs out.
data.title: The Fifth Element

data.description: Raised in a sterile underground complex, Lincoln Six Echo dreams of winning a lottery to idyllic “The Island.” When he learns the haven is a lie and he's an organ clone for wealthy sponsors, he flees with fellow clone Jordan. Chased by corporate security, they navigate the real world for the first time, fighting to expose a billion-dollar secret built on disposable human lives.
data.title: The Island

data.description: Lovable underachiever Ted hires a private eye to find his long-lost prom date Mary. The detective falls for her himself, lies multiply, and suitors collide in increasingly disastrous set pieces involving zipper accidents, hair gel infamy, and a relentless little dog. Amid gross-out gags, the film still roots for sincerity to win over competition and coincidence.
data.title: There's Something About Mary

data.description: After years apart, the gifted but dysfunctional Tenenbaum siblings return to their Manhattan brownstone when patriarch Royal claims he's dying. Old wounds resurface amid falcons, playhouse tents, and lacrosse trophies. Wes Anderson's pastel diorama blends deadpan humor and melancholy as the family fumbles toward forgiveness, proving that brilliance doesn't immunize anyone from heartbreak or hope.
data.title: The Royal Tenenbaums

data.description: Wrongly imprisoned banker Andy Dufresne endures decades inside Shawshank, carving chess pieces and befriending lifer Red while secretly funneling warden kickbacks. Library petitions, rock hammer patience, and a poster-covered tunnel lead to a rain-soaked escape and a promise on a Mexican beach, celebrating the quiet power of hope in a place built to crush it.
data.title: The Shawshank Redemption

data.description: Writer Jack Torrance takes his family to the isolated Overlook Hotel as winter caretaker, seeking quiet to finish a novel. Snowbound hallways whisper with ghosts, his psychic son sees rivers of blood, and Jack's mind fractures into homicidal madness. Kubrick's labyrinthine tracking shots and the cursed room 237 turn cabin fever into iconic horror about cycles of violence and possession.
data.title: The Shining

data.description: Child psychologist Malcolm Crowe takes on Cole, a boy who claims to see dead people. As Malcolm pieces together clues through whispered confidences, cold rooms, and ghostly apparitions, he confronts his own unresolved life. The climax's twist reframes every scene, turning this quiet thriller into a meditation on grief, listening, and the unseen burdens children carry.
data.title: The Sixth Sense

data.description: Talented grifter Tom Ripley is hired to retrieve wealthy playboy Dickie Greenleaf from Italy, but envy of Dickie's life curdles into obsession. Forged signatures, stolen passports, and Jazz Age parties in Naples give way to murder and impersonation as Tom scrambles to maintain his new identity while detectives circle and guilt eats at his carefully crafted mask.
data.title: The Talented Mr. Ripley

data.description: Five crooks brought together for a lineup spin an elaborate tale of a ship explosion and the elusive mastermind Keyser Soze. Flashbacks, unreliable narration, and a gold-laden heist build to a police interrogation where verbal tics and coffee cups hide the truth. The thriller hinges on how stories shape belief—and how the greatest trick is hiding in plain sight.
data.title: The Usual Suspects

data.description: In 1984 East Berlin, Stasi captain Gerd Wiesler is ordered to surveil a playwright suspected of dissent. As he listens to the writer's apartment, he becomes entwined in their lives and begins to question the regime he serves. Small acts of sabotage and compassion pit him against a system built on fear, illustrating how art and empathy can crack even the most disciplined loyalty.
data.title: Das Leben der Anderen

data.description: Mild-mannered dentist Nick “Oz” Oseransky discovers his new neighbor is Jimmy “The Tulip” Tudeski, a notorious hitman hiding out. Mobsters, vengeful wives, and a $10 million bounty swirl through suburban cul-de-sacs as Oz stammers through fake hits and real feelings for Jimmy's wife's friend. Crime, romance, and screwball misunderstandings prove suburbia can be deadlier than any city block.
data.title: The Whole Nine Yards

data.description: Sergeant Neil Howie arrives on the remote island of Summerisle to investigate a missing girl and finds a pagan community preparing for a May Day ritual. Clashing Christian faith with fertility rites, he is drawn into songs, masks, and bonfires that mask a gruesome plan. Folk horror tension builds toward a shocking wicker effigy finale that questions sacrifice, belief, and authority.
data.title: The Wicker Man
