data.description: Construction worker Douglas Quaid visits Rekall for virtual Mars memories and learns his life may itself be fabricated. Soon he's hunted by corporate goons, ally spies, and a tyrant controlling oxygen on the red planet. Mutant rebels and a reactor buried under Olympus Mons force Quaid to decide whether he's a hero named Hauser or just the pawn of someone else's implanted dream.
data.title: Total Recall

data.description: Heroin addict Mark Renton vows to quit Edinburgh's drug scene, but friendship with feckless Spud, volatile Begbie, and charming Sick Boy keeps pulling him back. Scams, overdoses, and the world's worst toilet compete with fleeting moments of clarity. A dangerous heroin deal offers escape money—if Renton can betray his mates and choose life over the chaos he's long romanticized.
data.title: Trainspotting

data.description: Hitman Ghost Dog follows an ancient samurai code while doing contract jobs for a small-time mobster. When the family turns on him to erase loose ends, Ghost Dog wages a solitary war with a silenced pistol, carrier pigeons, and Zen calm. Hip-hop beats, haiku, and urban decay frame a parable about loyalty, cultural fusion, and violence as personal philosophy.
data.title: Ghost Dog: Way of the Samurai

data.description: In near-future Britain ruled by a fascist regime, masked anarchist V wages vendetta with explosive spectacle and Shakespearean monologues. He rescues Evey, awakening her to resistance as his Guy Fawkes plan targets Parliament. Propaganda broadcasts, plague panic, and personal trauma collide in a story about whether ideas are bulletproof and what price people will pay to be free.
data.title: V for Vendetta

data.description: After the ice caps melt, drifter known as the Mariner sails a seaborne world trading dirt and avoiding human contact. When he rescues a woman and a tattooed girl holding the map to mythical Dryland, they're hunted by Smokers on jury-rigged jet skis. Sea battles, rusted tankers, and floating atolls fuel a post-apocalyptic quest for solid ground and a future beyond water.
data.title: Waterworld

data.description: Hacker Neo follows a white rabbit into a secret war, learning that his world is a machine-crafted simulation. With mentor Morpheus and fighter Trinity, he dodges bullet time, combats sentient Agents, and trains to become “The One” who can rewrite code from within. Cyberpunk set pieces question reality, freedom, and what humanity will risk to wake from a comfortable lie.
data.title: The Matrix

data.description: Oh Dae-su is abducted and locked in a private cell for 15 years with only a TV for company. Suddenly released, he hunts the captor who stole his life, armed with a hammer and a burning need for answers. Twisted vengeance, hypnosis, and a devastating final revelation blur justice and cruelty in Park Chan-wook's operatic thriller about memory and the cost of obsession.
data.title: Oldboy

data.description: Chicago mob fixer Ray Tango recounts one disastrous night when a contract hit unravels. Street hustlers, a jittery cabbie, and double-crossing gangsters collide in a chain of shootings and botched getaways. Noir narration and splintered loyalties paint a city where survival depends on instinct, luck, and knowing when to cut your losses—even if it means betraying the wrong man.
data.title: Sucker Free City

data.description: Conan hits the road to meet podcast fans in their home countries, turning awkward video-call friendships into in-person adventures. Across Norway, Argentina, Thailand, Ireland, Spain, New Zealand, and Austria, he mangles phrases, crashes family dinners, and jams with local bands, mixing sincere curiosity with self-deprecating chaos as travel mishaps and heartfelt conversations blur tourism with late-night comedy.
data.title: Conan O'Brien Must Go

data.description: Four New Yorkers—Jerry, George, Elaine, and Kramer—navigate minutiae that snowball into absurdity: waiting for tables, close-talkers, parking garages, puffy shirts, and contests of willpower. With stand-up interludes and circular plots, the “show about nothing” turns petty grievances into timeless farce, defining 1990s sitcom rhythm and inspiring countless observational comedies that followed.
data.title: Seinfeld

data.description: Larry David plays a prickly version of himself in improvised half hours where minor social slights ignite cascading disasters. From golf etiquette to cellphone etiquette, friends, exes, and celebrities become collateral damage in Larry's quest to obey—and weaponize—his own rules. Long arcs (a restaurant, a play, a legal trial) tie seasons together while each episode lands on one exquisitely awkward punchline.
data.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm

data.description: FBI agents Fox Mulder and Dana Scully chase aliens, mutants, and conspiracies while debating science versus belief. Monster-of-the-week chills intertwine with a sprawling mythology about government coverups and colonization. Noir lighting, Mark Snow's theme, and skeptical banter defined 1990s sci-fi TV, while two revival seasons proved that the truth—and chemistry between its leads—still isn't out there.
data.title: The X-Files

data.description: Air Force Colonel Jack O'Neill and archaeologist Daniel Jackson reopen the Stargate, forming SG-1 to explore distant worlds, battle parasitic Goa'uld tyrants, and ally with rebel Jaffa. Ten seasons blend military action, mythology, and dry humor, while a tight ensemble and case-of-the-week missions grow into galaxy-spanning politics that still make room for bottle episodes, time loops, and meta jokes.
data.title: Stargate SG-1

data.description: Intern J.D. joins Sacred Heart Hospital and narrates surreal daydreams, hard lessons, and found-family camaraderie with Turk, Elliot, and gruff mentor Dr. Cox. Comedic cutaways balance medical heartbreak as the staff wrestles with ego, empathy, and burnout. The series pioneered single-camera workplace dramedy long before streaming binges made “comfort rewatch” a genre of its own.
data.title: Scrubs

data.description: Brilliant but misanthropic Dr. Gregory House leads a diagnostic team that solves medical mysteries through deductive leaps, risky treatments, and plenty of Vicodin-laced sarcasm. Each case tests ethics and friendship while a rotating cast of fellows challenges House's worldview. Procedural puzzles meet character study, showing how genius and self-destruction coexist inside the same hoodie and limp.
data.title: House MD

data.description: Chef and author Anthony Bourdain travels from Beirut to Brooklyn night markets, eating with locals, cooks, and taxi drivers to reveal politics, history, and humor through food. The show's handheld style, punk soundtrack, and frank narration made it less a travel brochure than a culinary anthropology class, inspiring viewers to chase flavor over fine dining and empathy over clichés.
data.title: Anthony Bourdain: No Reservations

data.description: The Simpsons lampoons American life through the endlessly elastic town of Springfield. Homer's blunders, Marge's patience, Bart's pranks, Lisa's ideals, and Maggie's silence anchor stories that blend satire, slapstick, and heartfelt family beats. After three decades the series keeps morphing—HD animation, topical jokes, and meta milestones—while closing in on its 800th episode.
data.title: The Simpsons

data.description: A mockumentary lens follows paper company employees in Scranton where romance, pranks, and corporate downsizing collide. Jim and Pam's slow-burn love, Michael Scott's cringe leadership, Dwight's beet-powered ambition, and a deadpan camera crew turn mundane office life into comedic gold that also lands emotional gut punches about friendship, work, and finding meaning in a cubicle.
data.title: The Office

data.description: Leslie Knope's relentless optimism powers the Parks Department of Pawnee, Indiana, where bureaucratic headaches, waffles, and a tiny horse become civic religion. Deadpan Ron, sardonic April, eager Ben, and literal star-child Andy orbit Leslie's crusade to make government kind and competent, turning workplace mockumentary into a love letter to public service and chosen family.
data.title: Parks and Recreation

data.description: Burger slinger Bob Belcher, wife Linda, and kids Tina, Gene, and Louise scrape by running a seaside diner where landlord disputes, health inspections, and talent shows become musical, pun-laden adventures. With heartfelt chaos and running gags, the long-running animated sitcom has reached its 300th episode while keeping the Belchers' optimism, sibling scheming, and burger-of-the-day jokes sizzling.
data.title: Bob's Burgers

data.description: Anthology of techno-paranoia where each standalone episode imagines near-future worlds warped by screens, AI, social scores, or virtual immortality. Season 7 (2025) brought the total to 33 tales, including the first sequel “USS Callister: Into Infinity.” Dark satire, horror, and bleak humor expose how human frailties, not gadgets, make our black mirrors reflect the worst—and sometimes the best—of us.
data.title: Black Mirror

data.description: Oldest brother Francis off at military school, middle-child Malcolm narrates growing up in a chaotic, genius-level family where IQ points don't equal social skills. Surreal cutaways, relentless parents Lois and Hal, and brotherly schemes balance slapstick with sharp insights about class and adolescence, making this single-camera comedy a cornerstone of early-2000s coming-of-age TV.
data.title: Malcolm In The Middle

data.description: Baltimore's drug trade, police department, schools, docks, city hall, and newsroom intertwine in this five-season tapestry. Each year shifts focus while showing how institutions grind down individuals like cops McNulty and Bunk, dealer-turned-student Michael, and teachers trying to save kids. The Wire uses patient, novelistic storytelling to expose systemic failure without easy heroes.
data.title: The Wire

data.description: Chef Gordon Ramsay storms into failing restaurants, tasting awful food, confronting denial, and enforcing brutal honesty. Over a week he rewrites menus, refreshes décor, and drills kitchens into shape while exposing the human drama behind every bad balance sheet. Equal parts makeover, business bootcamp, and tough-love therapy, the series made “It's RAW!” a meme and saved many small-town eateries.
data.title: Kitchen Nightmares

data.description: A true-crime anthology that reinvents itself each season: from Minnesota snowdrifts to Kansas wheat fields and 2019 Hollywood, ordinary Midwesterners stumble into murders, coverups, and karmic coincidences. Coen-esque humor, baroque monologues, and morally gray cops collide with crime families and drifters, proving that fate, bad weather, and one bad decision can rewrite entire lives.
data.title: Fargo

data.description: Cartman, Stan, Kyle, and Kenny skewer everything from politics to pop culture in a Colorado mountain town where musical numbers, aliens, and foul-mouthed school assemblies coexist. Stone and Parker's rapid six-day production keeps episodes hyper-current, while nearly three decades of chaos—plus specials and movies—have turned construction-paper satire into one of TV's longest-running animated comedies.
data.title: South Park

data.description: The Griffin family—Peter, Lois, Meg, Chris, Stewie, and talking dog Brian—careen through cutaway gags, musical spoofs, and dark punchlines in Quahog, Rhode Island. Surreal side jokes, meta humor, and pop-culture riffs fuel this long-running animated sitcom, which has evolved from cult cancellation to a 400-plus-episode fixture of Sunday-night satire.
data.title: Family Guy

data.description: Pizza delivery boy Fry wakes up 1,000 years in the future working for Planet Express alongside one-eyed captain Leela, kleptomaniac robot Bender, and a menagerie of lovable weirdos. The series blends sharp sci-fi ideas, math jokes, and heartfelt tearjerkers (“Jurassic Bark,” “Luck of the Fryrish”) across cancellations and revivals, proving animated sitcoms can make you cry between laughs.
data.title: Futurama

data.description: Five narcissistic friends run the worst Irish bar in Philadelphia, hatching schemes that weaponize selfishness—welfare fraud, musical pageants, fake charities, and endless debates about who is the Golden God. Shot handheld with improv energy, the show pushes sitcom taboos while revealing just enough humanity to keep the gang's self-destruction hilariously watchable 170 episodes in.
data.title: It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia

data.description: Radio psychiatrist Frasier Crane returns to Seattle, juggling a new talk show, his retired cop dad, perfectionist brother Niles, and live-in aide Daphne. Wit, opera references, and farce play out in high-rise apartments and radio booths. An acclaimed reboot in 2023 adds a 12th season to the original 11, proving urbane wordplay and familial neurosis still resonate decades later.
data.title: Frasier

data.description: In Silicon Valley, coder Richard Hendricks founds Pied Piper to compress data better than tech giants. Every win triggers new investors, lawsuits, and pivots as his awkward team battles billionaires with ruthless NDAs. The satire skewers startup hype, venture capital egos, and ethical gray zones while celebrating the rare moments when engineering idealism beats greed—at least until the next sprint.
data.title: Silicon Valley

data.description: Propane salesman Hank Hill tries to keep traditional values alive in Arlen, Texas, as family, neighbors, and pocket sand complicate his quiet life. Son Bobby's odd hobbies, Peggy's confidence, and Dale's conspiracies fuel gentle satire of suburban America. Over 13 seasons, the show blended warmth and deadpan humor, becoming a benchmark for character-driven animated sitcoms.
data.title: King of the Hill

data.description: Stop-motion action figures parody blockbusters, toys, and late-night infomercials at breakneck speed. From “G.I. Jogger” to the never-ending Emperor phone call, sketches skewer pop culture with clay blood and absurd crossovers. Eleven seasons plus specials show how a basement full of dolls can turn into one of Adult Swim's most prolific, anarchic sketch factories.
data.title: Robot Chicken

data.description: Three cartoon housemates—a fame-hungry actress, a video-game barbarian, and a hygiene-averse internet icon—live in a reality-show fishbowl that gleefully offends everyone. Confessionals, manufactured challenges, and raunchy gags parody MTV tropes while letting anarchic animation push boundaries live-action couldn't. Short-lived but notorious, the series crammed two and a half seasons with unapologetic shock humor.
data.title: Drawn Together

data.description: In 1980s Hawkins, Indiana, a missing boy leads his friends to a psychic girl named Eleven, Russian plots beneath a mall, and a carnivorous realm called the Upside Down. Each season escalates from bike rides and D&D to mall invasions and cursed videotapes, blending Spielbergian nostalgia with Lovecraft dread while the kids, now teens, learn that growing up can be scarier than any monster.
data.title: Stranger Things

data.description: Former military policeman Jack Reacher drifts across America with nothing but a toothbrush and a bruiser's frame, solving murders by reading footprints, punching math into goons, and outthinking small-town corruption. Each season adapts a Lee Child novel, mixing detective puzzles, deadpan humor, and kinetic brawls where leverage, not bullets, decides who walks away.
data.title: Reacher

data.description: Two centuries before Daenerys, the Targaryen dynasty fractures over succession, pitting dragonriders Rhaenyra and Aegon against kin and councils. Court whispers spark wildfire-scale battles in the air and the Small Council chamber alike. Lavish sets, Valyrian lore, and looming prophecy show how personal slights ignite wars that will reshape Westeros long before a certain throne is melted.
data.title: House of the Dragon

data.description: Surgical intern Meredith Grey arrives at Seattle Grace and grows into a trailblazing surgeon while friendships, romances, and traumas stack up like charts. Plane crashes, pandemics, and hospital mergers push doctors to their limits as new cohorts replace old favorites. The long-running medical drama balances soap operatics with ethical dilemmas in the OR across two decades of television history.
data.title: Grey's Anatomy

data.description: Alien ships hover silently over Earth, triggering fragmented invasions in Japan, the US, and Syria. Scientists, soldiers, and parents scramble to decode motives while the enemy adapts. The Apple TV+ drama lingers on human cost—grief, trust, and resilience—mixing intimate character arcs with slow-burn sci-fi tension across continents as humanity learns it may not be the dominant species anymore.
data.title: Invasion

data.description: BAU profilers chase America's worst predators, reading crime scenes like biographies of the killers. Rotating teams from Gideon to Prentiss build geographic and psychological profiles, racing against ticking clocks and their own burnout. After 15 seasons, the series rebirthed as Evolution with darker serialized arcs, proving the fascination—and toll—of staring into the abyss hasn't faded.
data.title: Criminal Minds

data.description: Based on Liu Cixin's trilogy, scientists and gamers receive a countdown from the stars, leading to past Cultural Revolution tragedies, a secret VR world, and the revelation that an alien fleet is en route. As physics bends and factions form, humanity must unify or be cataloged by a civilization that sees Earth as a problem to manage, not a planet to negotiate with.
data.title: 3 Body Problem

data.description: Teen addict Rue narrates love, relapse, and identity crises among Gen-Z classmates balancing euphoria and despair. Social media glare, opioid ghosts, and glitter-soaked parties collide with tender friendships and betrayal. Stylized cinematography and fearless performances make the HBO drama a raw, empathetic study of growing up wired, watched, and desperately searching for belonging.
data.title: Euphoria

data.description: Struggling chemistry teacher Walter White turns to cooking meth after a cancer diagnosis, dragging former student Jesse Pinkman into a criminal empire. As the blue product spreads, lies, violence, and ego transform Walt from family man into Heisenberg, shattering everyone in his orbit. Five seasons of meticulous plotting made this a landmark of tension, morality, and antihero storytelling.
data.title: Breaking Bad

data.description: Years after Miami's Bay Harbor Butcher vanished, Dexter Morgan resurfaces, drawn back into forensics and fatherhood when a copycat spree threatens to expose his code. Haunted by ghosts old and new, he must decide whether to embrace the monster or bury it for good. The sequel revival picks up the scalpel with older, harsher consequences and a city that has learned from his legend.
data.title: Dexter: Resurrection

data.description: Survivors of Oceanic Flight 815 crash on a mysterious Pacific island where smoke monsters, hatches, and time flashes test their sanity. As past lives intersect with island fate, the group battles Others, dharma experiments, and themselves. The ambitious ensemble drama mixed pulp adventure with philosophical mystery, pioneering binge-worthy, puzzle-box TV across six twisty seasons.
data.title: Lost

data.description: CIA officer Carrie Mathison suspects turned POW Nicholas Brody of plotting terror, igniting a cat-and-mouse saga that expands into global espionage. The series pairs pulse-pounding operations with intimate looks at loyalty, mental health, and political compromise. Across eight seasons it shifts from DC to Islamabad and Moscow, questioning what patriotism costs in a forever war.
data.title: Homeland

data.description: New Jersey mob boss Tony Soprano juggles panic attacks, therapy sessions, and brutal business. Family dinners, ducks in his pool, and feuds with rival crews expose the cost of power and the fragility beneath his swagger. Six seasons of morally rich storytelling ushered in TV's golden age, proving gangster epics could also be intimate studies of anxiety, loyalty, and identity.
data.title: The Sopranos

data.description: Top Chef gathers ambitious chefs in a pressure-cooker kitchen gauntlet: quickfires at dawn, restaurant wars at midnight, and judges who will send anyone home for broken sauces or cold plates. Moving city to city each season, it blends culinary craft, strategic alliances, and travelogue-worthy ingredient hunts, creating a decade-spanning showcase for rising stars and unforgettable blunders.
data.title: Top Chef

data.description: In Hell's Kitchen, chef Gordon Ramsay drills aspiring line cooks through blistering dinner services, humiliating raw scallops and applauding perfect risottos. Teams swap jackets, sabotage rivals, and fight for a head-chef prize while Ramsay's tirades and surprise challenges expose who can lead a brigade under fire and who will hang up their black jacket.
data.title: Hell's Kitchen

data.description: Amateur bakers enter a tent in the British countryside to face signature, technical, and showstopper challenges judged with gentle rigor. Melting chocolate, collapsing sponges, and Hollywood handshakes create weekly suspense, while the camaraderie, pastoral vibes, and quietly savage “soggy bottom” critiques make this baking competition as wholesome as it is exacting.
data.title: The Great British Bake Off

data.description: Home cooks battle through mystery boxes and restaurant takeovers under the glare of exacting judges. MasterChef turns pantry creativity and plating finesse into weekly eliminations, blending heart-tugging backstories with ruthless critiques. Winners leave with cash, a cookbook deal, and proof that amateur passion can stand alongside professional skill.
data.title: MasterChef

data.description: Host Guy Fieri crisscrosses America in a red Camaro, spotlighting mom-and-pop joints where barbecue smoke, stacked sandwiches, and secret sauces rule. Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives celebrates regional specialties through sizzling griddles, back-of-house tours, and the stories of families keeping neighborhood flavors alive, turning roadside grease into appointment viewing.
data.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives

data.description: Chefs try to dethrone Iron Chef champ Bobby Flay in a two-round sprint: first beating a peer to earn the right to challenge him, then facing Bobby on a surprise signature ingredient. Blind tastings decide if the upstart's dish can outshine Flay's mastery, making each episode a compact culinary duel of speed, strategy, and swagger.
data.title: Beat Bobby Flay

data.description: Chef's Table serves cinematic portraits of world-class chefs—from Modena to Bangkok—lingering on smoke, sauce, and philosophy. Each episode pairs slow-motion kitchens with the personal histories, failures, and obsessions behind a signature dish, redefining food TV as arthouse biography where flavor, memory, and culture share the same plate.
data.title: Chef's Table

data.description: Guy's Grocery Games turns a supermarket into an obstacle course where chefs dash aisles for ingredients, spin culinary wheel challenges, and cook under bizarre constraints like five-item baskets or cooking with only middle-aisle goods. The show blends competition frenzy with budget hacks, reminding viewers that great meals can start with whatever a cart can carry.
data.title: Guy's Grocery Games

data.description: Bon Appétit's test kitchen team—editors, chefs, and food nerds—experiment on camera, perfecting recipes while revealing the flops, science, and jokes in between. From gourmet candy re-creations to weeknight pasta drills, the series made process as addictive as results, inspiring home cooks to chase technique, not just trends.
data.title: Bon Appétit

data.description: Your Majesty follows elite pastry teams crafting royal-themed desserts for stately banquets and whimsical crown challenges. Sugar palaces, chocolate thrones, and gravity-defying sponge sculptures are judged on elegance and flavor, turning classical pâtisserie into competitive pageantry where one wobble can topple an edible monarchy.
data.title: Your Majesty

data.description: Next Level Baker stacks three kitchens—basement, mid-level, and top-tier—where pastry chefs rotate stations based on performance. Constrained pantries, surprise twists, and brutal time cuts force creativity under pressure, turning buttercream and laminated dough into tactical weapons as contestants climb (or tumble down) the culinary ladder each episode.
data.title: Next Level Baker

data.description: America's Test Kitchen methodically reverse-engineers recipes, testing dozens of variations to deliver foolproof results. Blind tastings, equipment reviews, and science explainers turn home cooking into approachable R&D, empowering viewers with techniques rather than trends across hundreds of half-hour episodes filmed in an ever-busier Boston kitchen.
data.title: America's Test Kitchen

data.description: Anthony Bourdain roams 80 cities on Parts Unknown, eating in markets, war zones, and family kitchens to map culture through flavor. The series mixes handheld meals, jazz scores, and candid politics, showing how food reveals memory, conflict, and resilience—whether at a Hanoi bun cha stall or a West Virginia diner shuttered by opioid grief.
data.title: Anthony Bourdain: Parts Unknown

data.description: Hot Ones flips the talk-show formula: guests answer increasingly personal questions while eating chicken wings coated in escalating hot sauces. As Scoville levels soar, celebrities sweat, swear, and occasionally achieve enlightenment, proving that a cleverly structured gimmick can coax candid stories and viral reactions in under 30 minutes.
data.title: Hot Ones

data.description: Gordon Ramsay: Uncharted sends the chef into remote regions—Peru's Andes, Louisiana bayous, Icelandic fjords—to learn indigenous techniques, forage wild ingredients, and duel local masters in a final cookoff. Part travelogue, part survival, it spotlights culinary traditions often overlooked by luxury dining and shows Ramsay humbled, climbing, and even spear fishing to earn each plate.
data.title: Gordon Ramsay: Uncharted

data.description: In the lawless Outer Rim after the Empire's fall, lone bounty hunter Din Djarin protects Force-sensitive Grogu while dodging Imperial remnants, rival guilds, and Mandalorian politics. Each chapter blends gunslinger duels, creature hunts, and quiet father-son moments, expanding Star Wars lore with found family, beskar honor codes, and lore-shifting cameos that tie the galaxy far, far away together.
data.title: The Mandalorian

data.description: A love letter and lampoon to classic Trek, The Orville follows Captain Ed Mercer and crew on exploratory missions that veer from first-contact diplomacy to time paradoxes and satire of 21st-century culture. Humor shares equal screen time with ethical quandaries, heartfelt character beats, and surprisingly ambitious sci-fi plots across episodic adventures and serialized arcs.
data.title: The Orville

data.description: Set 10,000 years before Paul Atreides, Bene Gesserit sisters navigate the brutal politics of the Imperium, honing prana-bindu control and seeding bloodlines that will birth the Kwisatz Haderach. Intrigue on Wallach IX, feuds with Houses, and whispered witchcraft collide as the order learns that power over spice is power over destiny itself.
data.title: Dune: Prophecy

data.description: Nurse Claire Randall slips from 1945 into 1743 Scotland, where clan wars, Jacobite plots, and a romance with Highlander Jamie Fraser upend her marriage and modern ethics. Spanning continents and decades, the saga weaves time travel with medical dilemmas, political rebellions, and an enduring love tested by history's cruelties and miracles.
data.title: Outlander

data.description: After xenomorph sightings are dismissed as myth, an investigative team on a rapidly industrializing Earth uncovers biocorp conspiracies, ancient Engineer tech, and a hive hidden beneath a megacity. Survival horror meets hard sci-fi as Weyland-Yutani factions race to weaponize the ultimate organism, forcing unlikely allies to choose between profit, species survival, and their own humanity.
data.title: Alien: Earth

data.description: In a silo 144 stories underground, survivors obey rigid rules that ban talk of the outside. Engineer Juliette probes a murder and uncovers censored logs, faulty sensors, and a conspiracy about why humanity was buried. The taut dystopian thriller mixes locked-room mystery with world-building that peels away secrets level by level, asking what truth is worth when it threatens survival.
data.title: Silo

data.description: Genius drunk Rick drags anxious grandson Morty across multiverses, where Cronenberg mutations, Council of Ricks politics, and sentient pickles normalize existential dread. Behind the nihilist jokes lies sharp sci-fi riffing and surprising heart as the Smith family navigates divorce, clones, and cosmic crises over 70 episodes of animated chaos.
data.title: Rick and Morty

data.description: When humanity's last hope lies aboard Ark One, a deep-space catastrophe kills most of the senior crew, leaving young officers to navigate sabotage, dwindling resources, and unknown threats on the way to a new colony. The Syfy thriller leans on ensemble tension and closed-corridor stakes, asking whether leadership forged in crisis can outrun the dangers waiting in uncharted space.
data.title: The Ark

data.description: In a colonized solar system, a cop on Ceres, a jaded freighter crew, and a UN diplomat uncover a conspiracy involving alien protomolecule that could rewrite life itself. Hard science, tense ship combat, and political intrigue between Earth, Mars, and the Belt drive six seasons of meticulously built world-building that made space feel both vast and perilously human.
data.title: The Expanse

data.description: A shimmering dome seals Chester's Mill off from the world, cutting power, supply lines, and sanity. Residents scramble for leadership, resources, and answers as the barrier reveals strange properties and a possible alien origin. The sci-fi thriller turns small-town dramas into pressure-cooker conflicts where secrets and survival instincts collide over three chaotic seasons.
data.title: Under the Dome

data.description: Saitama trained so hard he went bald—and now defeats any foe with a single punch, leaving him crushingly bored. In a world of kaiju attacks, hero rankings, and cyborg sidekicks, he seeks a worthy challenge while Genos, the Hero Association, and villains like the Sea King test whether limitless power can still find purpose, humor, and humanity.
data.title: One-Punch Man

data.description: Pirate dreamer Monkey D. Luffy sails the Grand Line with a straw-hatted crew of misfits to find the legendary One Piece and become King of the Pirates. Thousand Sunny adventures juggle rubber-powered battles, found-family bonds, and massive worldbuilding—Warlords, Marines, Yonko—spanning islands of sky, fishmen, and samurai over an ever-growing ocean of episodes.
data.title: One Piece

data.description: In a world where 80% of people have superpowers called Quirks, powerless Midoriya Izuku inherits One For All and enters U.A. High to learn heroics. Training arcs, sports festivals, villain wars, and ethical dilemmas pit Class 1-A against foes like Shigaraki and All For One, examining what makes a true hero when society itself teeters between hope and fear.
data.title: My Hero Academia

data.description: Set between Judgment Day and the war with Skynet, Terminator Zero follows survivors in 1990s Tokyo as sentient machines manipulate timelines to ensure AI ascendance. A hacker, a soldier from the future, and a reprogrammed Terminator race against annihilation, blending noir intrigue, anime aesthetics, and the franchise's central question: can humanity outthink the future it created?
data.title: Terminator Zero

data.description: After two years of training, Naruto returns to Konoha ready to rescue Sasuke and face Akatsuki. Shippūden tracks the Fourth Great Ninja War, tailed beast politics, and Naruto's path to Hokage, weaving huge battle set pieces with themes of legacy, chosen burdens, and friendship that survives betrayal across 500 fast-paced, chakra-charged episodes.
data.title: Naruto: Shippūden

data.description: Goku and friends face gods of destruction, multiverse tournaments, and reality-breaking fusions. Dragon Ball Super escalates from Beerus's challenge to the Tournament of Power and the Broly clash, delivering power-ups like Super Saiyan Blue and Ultra Instinct while keeping humor, training, and classic rivalries alive across 131 kinetic episodes.
data.title: Dragon Ball Super

data.description: Trainer Ash Ketchum (Satoshi) journeys through regions from Kanto to Paldea with Pikachu, challenging gyms, battling rivals, and forging friendships with ever-expanding companions and Pokémon species. The globe-trotting anime mixes adventure, humor, and coming-of-age lessons across more than two decades of leagues, movies, and farewells, proving that the quest to “catch 'em all” is really about growing up.
data.title: Pokémon

data.description: Orphan Xiao Yan loses his powers, then gains a mentor and a mystical ring that kickstart his climb through the Dou Qi ranks. Facing clan intrigue, alchemists, and demonic beasts, he tempers talent with hard-forged discipline. The Chinese 3D donghua adapts the xianxia novel into sweeping cultivation battles and romance across multiple seasons of fiery duels and pill refining.
data.title: Battle Through the Heavens

data.description: Genius student Light Yagami gains a Death Note that kills anyone whose name he writes. As he executes criminals to build a new world, detective L leads a cerebral cat-and-mouse duel that spirals into moral gray zones, fake rules, and successor prodigies. The thriller explores justice, power, and corruption in 37 tightly wound episodes where every move could be fatal.
data.title: Death Note

data.description: Class 3-E must assassinate their homeroom teacher—a tentacled superbeing who plans to destroy Earth after graduation—while he teaches them study habits and self-worth. Assassination Classroom balances slapstick training with heartfelt growth as misfit students discover talent under impossible pressure, turning a wild premise into a surprisingly sincere tale of mentorship and second chances.
data.title: Ansatsu Kyoushitsu (Assassination Classroom)

data.description: Guts the Black Swordsman swings an iron slab of a blade across a world of apostles, demonic eclipses, and corrupt kings. Haunted by the Band of the Hawk's betrayal, he travels with witch Schierke and cursed lover Casca, battling fate itself. The dark fantasy fuses brutal combat with meditations on trauma and free will, continuing a legendary manga's bleak, operatic saga.
data.title: Berserk

data.description: Demon hunter Dante runs a debt-ridden freelance shop, taking jobs that pit his pistols and sword against hellspawn threatening the human world. Stylish gunplay, wisecracks, and gothic rock flair translate the Capcom games into episodic exorcisms that hint at Dante's family tragedy while keeping every mission a monster-of-the-week thrill ride.
data.title: Devil May Cry

data.description: In a world where spontaneous human combustion creates fire demons, Special Fire Force Company 8 battles Infernals while uncovering the Evangelist's plot to trigger a cataclysm. Rookie Shinra “Devil's Footprints” Kusakabe seeks to clear his family name, navigating squad rivalries, kinetic firefights, and lore about Adolla Bursts that could ignite or save what's left of humanity.
data.title: Fire Force

data.description: Genial schemer Miyuki Shirogane and proud heiress Kaguya Shinomiya wage psychological war to make the other confess first, turning student council meetings into rom-com battlefields. Deadpan narration, split-screen mind games, and sudden slapstick elevate each near-confession, while friends Chika and Ishigami add chaos. Beneath the tactics lies a tender look at teenage pride and longing.
data.title: Kaguya-sama: Love is War

data.description: Warring states in ancient China come alive as orphan Xin (Shin) fights from foot soldier to Great General under King Ying Zheng. Sweeping battles, political schemes, and brutal duels chart the unification of Qin, showing camaraderie, sacrifice, and strategy across massive animated campaigns that balance history with high-stakes shōnen energy.
data.title: Kingdom

data.description: When a dungeon collapses and the party's leader is eaten by a red dragon, his sister Laios heads back down with a mismatched crew, determined to rescue him before digestion finishes. They survive by cooking the monsters they fight—basilisk steaks, walking mushroom stews—turning classic fantasy crawls into a cozy culinary adventure where strategy, flavor, and friendship keep everyone alive.
data.title: Delicious in Dungeon

data.description: NYPD's Special Victims Unit investigates sex crimes and abuse cases that demand empathy as much as forensics. Veteran detective Olivia Benson leads rotating partners through interrogations, court prep, and undercover stings while wrestling with trauma and systemic bias. Two decades on, its ripped-from-the-headlines cases and courtroom payoffs make it the longest-running U.S. primetime drama.
data.title: Law & Order: Special Victims Unit

data.description: LA defense attorney Mickey Haller works from the backseat of a Lincoln, taking cases that range from cartel trials to tech-billionaire murders. Haunted by addiction yet powered by courtroom charisma, he juggles ex-wives on his payroll, a loyal driver, and a ruthless DA, proving that reasonable doubt often rides on hustle as much as legal precedent.
data.title: The Lincoln Lawyer

data.description: Folksy Atlanta defense lawyer Ben Matlock charges $100,000 per case, then out-thinks prosecutors with courtroom showmanship and meticulous cross-exams. Each murder-of-the-week hinges on spotting a contradiction others miss. Behind Matlock's seersucker suits are family ties, loyal P.I.s, and a belief that truth can be staged before a jury if you know where to dig.
data.title: Matlock

data.description: Ex-con lawyer Jimmy McGill slowly transforms into Saul Goodman, “criminal” attorney for the underworld. From elder-law scams to cartel money laundering, the prequel traces brotherly betrayal, love for Kim Wexler, and moral erosion. Meticulous visuals, desert cons, and courtroom feints show how the pursuit of success can warp talent into tragedy.
data.title: Better Call Saul

data.description: Chicago prosecutor Rusty Sabich is accused of murdering a colleague he loved. As DNA evidence, office politics, and family secrets surface, Rusty battles to prove innocence while doubting his own memory. The limited series reimagines Turow's thriller as a tense legal whodunit where every ally may be an adversary and justice could condemn the wrong man.
data.title: Presumed Innocent

data.description: College dropout Mike Ross talks his way into a job with closer Harvey Specter, bluffing a Harvard law degree. While hiding the secret, they win cases with swagger, pop-culture riffs, and creative settlements. Office politics, romance, and a looming bar scandal drive nine seasons of slick, character-driven legal drama set in a hyper-stylized Manhattan firm.
data.title: Suits

data.description: Each standalone episode of Accused begins with a defendant in court; flashbacks unravel how ordinary choices spiraled into alleged crimes. The anthology tackles hot-button issues—justice bias, online shaming, vigilante impulses—asking viewers to decide guilt before the verdict drops. Its rotating casts and moral gray zones keep every hour a fresh ethical debate.
data.title: Accused

data.description: Cold Justice follows former prosecutor Kelly Siegler and retired detective Yolanda McClary as they reopen small-town cold cases. With local cops, modern forensics, and dogged interviews, they hunt overlooked leads and push DA offices toward indictments. Real-world stakes and raw emotion make each solved case feel like justice arriving years late but not denied.
data.title: Cold Justice

data.description: Young idealists join the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York, handling terrorism, corruption, and Wall Street fraud. Mentored by a tough chief, they balance moral clarity with political realities, courtroom setbacks, and personal entanglements, dramatizing how justice is forged case by case inside America's most powerful district.
data.title: For the People

data.description: Down-and-out lawyer Billy McBride sues a giant defense contractor, igniting a gritty legal war that spans four seasons of corruption, addiction, and redemption. Each case exposes another rotten corner of corporate or political power as Billy, fueled by guilt and whiskey, cobbles together underdog teams to outwit firms with limitless resources.
data.title: Goliath

data.description: Alicia Florrick returns to the law after her husband's public sex-and-corruption scandal, rebuilding a career while navigating office politics, Chicago power brokers, and evolving tech ethics. Case-of-the-week trials mix with serialized arcs about surveillance, elections, and marriage, creating a sophisticated legal drama that balances sharp wit with moral ambiguity.
data.title: The Good Wife

data.description: Night Court's overnight shift handles New York's strangest cases—nudists, pickpockets, and magicians—under the irreverent gavel of Judge Harry Stone. With a sardonic prosecutor, big-hearted public defender, and towering bailiff Bull, the sitcom blends slapstick with warmth, showing that justice after dark can be weirdly wholesome.
data.title: Night Court

data.description: Judge Judy Sheindlin brings Bronx-honed bluntness to small-claims disputes over roommates, pets, and unpaid loans. Her rapid-fire bench rulings, eye rolls, and moral lectures made daytime arbitration must-watch TV for 25 seasons, proving that common sense, a clerk's notepad, and a withering stare can dispose of dockets faster than any gavel swing.
data.title: Judge Judy

data.description: At Crane, Poole & Schmidt, eccentric superstar attorneys Alan Shore and Denny Crane win impossible cases with wit, bombast, and occasional mad-cow digressions. Courtroom fireworks tackle tobacco, biotech, and civil liberties, while balcony cigars frame a friendship both absurd and profound. Boston Legal mixes sharp legal issues with outrageous comedy and sudden pathos.
data.title: Boston Legal

data.description: Little Fires Everywhere entwines the lives of journalist Elena Richardson and artist Mia Warren in 1990s Shaker Heights. A custody battle over an adopted baby ignites class, race, and motherhood tensions, revealing the secrets each woman hides. The miniseries layers slow-burn legal fights with domestic suspense, asking what “perfect” families will risk to stay intact.
data.title: Little Fires Everywhere

data.description: L.A. prosecutor Maya Travis returns to retry a movie star she believes got away with murder eight years prior. As evidence twists and her reputation hangs on a second shot, she battles media spin, ruthless defense counsel, and doubts inside her own office. The Fix blends courtroom maneuvers with noirish Los Angeles intrigue in a single-season thriller.
data.title: The Fix

data.description: HBO's Perry Mason reimagines the famed defense lawyer as a down-on-his-luck PI in 1932 Los Angeles, drawn into a child kidnapping case that exposes police corruption, evangelical empires, and his own scars from the Great War. Gritty period detail, noir mood, and courtroom reinvention show how Mason becomes the champion of the unjustly accused.
data.title: Perry Mason

data.description: Young lawyer Ellen Parsons joins ruthless litigator Patty Hewes, only to discover cases are battlegrounds where partners are expendable. Each season unfolds one major suit—corporate fraud, Ponzi schemes, whistleblowers—using flash-forwards that tease betrayals and body counts. Damages is a tense legal thriller about ambition's price and mentors who weaponize loyalty.
data.title: Damages

data.description: Set in a Pittsburgh teaching hospital, The Pitt follows a diverse residency class balancing brutal rotations, blue-collar patients, and research ambitions. Budget cuts, union debates, and transplant ethics collide with friendships and rivalries forged over 36-hour shifts. The series highlights how regional hospitals innovate under pressure while young doctors learn that medicine is as political as it is clinical.
data.title: The Pitt

data.description: Chicago Med follows the city's newest state-of-the-art trauma center, where Dr. Will Halstead, Dr. Ethan Choi, and colleagues juggle mass-casualty codes, gang-violence wounds, and tangled romances. Linked to the One Chicago universe, cases often cross with police and fire crews, showing how frontline teams coordinate under relentless pressure and dwindling resources.
data.title: Chicago Med

data.description: In 1950s East London, midwives at Nonnatus House bicycle through cobbled streets delivering babies, confronting poverty, racism, and evolving medical norms. Orders of nuns work alongside secular nurses as the NHS is born, blending gentle period detail with social-issue storytelling. Annual Christmas specials and ongoing seasons keep the drama intimate, hopeful, and grounded in community care.
data.title: Call the Midwife

data.description: In Watson, Dr. John Watson reinvents himself as a medical detective after Sherlock Holmes's death, blending trauma medicine with deductive logic. Each case fuses autopsy evidence, psychological insight, and battlefield triage while Watson confronts grief, celebrity, and copycat sleuths. The series re-centers the classic sidekick as lead, testing whether loyalty can outlive the legend it served.
data.title: Watson

data.description: Brilliant Minds (formerly Dr. Wolfe) centers on a revolutionary neurologist and her elite team treating rare brain disorders with cutting-edge tech and audacious surgeries. As they decode consciousness and identity, office politics, FDA battles, and patient consent test how far genius should push. The series mixes medical puzzles with ethical landmines and a dash of workplace romance.
data.title: Brilliant Minds

data.description: Best Medicine is a dramedy about a failing rural clinic that crowdsources innovation—3D-printed casts, telehealth, barter economies—to keep doors open. A burnt-out doc, a hacker nurse, and a newly minted PA juggle quirky patients and bureaucratic hurdles, proving that improvisation and community can be lifesaving tools when budgets and bandwidth run dry.
data.title: Best Medicine

data.description: ER drops viewers into frenetic Chicago County General shifts where Dr. Greene, Carter, Hathaway, and Benton race between trauma bays, juggling love, loss, and ever-evolving medicine. Handheld cameras and real-time codes pioneered the modern medical drama, spanning 15 seasons of pandemics, helicopter crashes, and ethical quandaries that influenced every hospital show that followed.
data.title: ER

data.description: Autistic savant Dr. Shaun Murphy joins San Jose St. Bonaventure Hospital, where photographic memory and pattern recognition make him a gifted surgeon-in-training. He must earn colleagues' trust while confronting bias, loss, and the relentless pace of modern medicine. The series mixes heartfelt character work with inventive surgical puzzles and ongoing debates about accommodation and excellence.
data.title: The Good Doctor

data.description: Nurses follows five young Canadian nurses navigating night shifts, code blues, and personal upheavals in a fast-paced Toronto hospital. Balancing burnout, friendships, and moral dilemmas, the series spotlights nursing as frontline problem-solving, showing how compassion, triage instincts, and teamwork keep a strained system running when seconds decide outcomes.
data.title: Nurses

data.description: Australian transplant doctor Frankie Bell returns home after a kidney transplant saves her life, only to face overcrowded wards, ticking clocks, and her own mortality as she treats patients. Pulse pairs high-stakes medicine with questions about identity, second chances, and whether saving others can redeem a life borrowed from a donor.
data.title: Pulse

data.description: Code Black drops residents into the nation's busiest ER, where patient surges outnumber staff and resources. Under the watch of Dr. Leanne Rorish, doctors learn to improvise life-saving care amid black-tag chaos, hospital politics, and grief. The series underscores how triage becomes moral calculus when every hallway is a battlefield.
data.title: Code Black

data.description: At Chastain Park Memorial, idealistic resident Devon Pravesh and renegade senior resident Conrad Hawkins expose billing fraud, device kickbacks, and administrative rot while still fighting to save patients. The Resident mixes romance and suspense with takedowns of a profit-driven system, arguing that heroism sometimes means defying protocol to do what's right.
data.title: The Resident

data.description: When FBI anthropologist Dr. Temperance “Bones” Brennan teams with war veteran Agent Seeley Booth, skeletal remains become stories that reveal killers. Each case mixes forensic science, pop-culture quips, and slow-burn romance, while Brennan's rational worldview clashes with Booth's gut instinct. Over twelve seasons, the Jeffersonian team proves bones rarely lie, but people often do.
data.title: Bones

data.description: Doc Martin follows Dr. Martin Ellingham, a gifted London surgeon turned grumpy village GP in Portwenn after developing a fear of blood. His brusque bedside manner collides with quirky locals and on-again, off-again romance with schoolteacher Louisa. Gentle humor, seaside scenery, and heartfelt cases show how community can soften even the sharpest scalpel.
data.title: Doc Martin

data.description: A superyacht's crew serves charter guests on the Med, juggling fine dining, tight quarters, and romantic entanglements while captains enforce maritime order. Each charter brings demanding clients, water-toy mishaps, and galley meltdowns, turning every turnaround day into a race against the clock. Seasons hop ports from Croatia to Malta, making luxury hospitality and nautical drama crash together below deck.
data.title: Below Deck Mediterranean

data.description: Americans leave home to build lives abroad with partners they've been dating long-distance, navigating visas in reverse. Culture clashes, language gaps, skeptical families, and tight budgets test whether love survives outside the U.S. Comfort zones shrink as couples juggle bureaucracy with weddings, making each season a reminder that romance requires resilience as much as romance.
data.title: 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way

data.description: Pickers Mike Wolfe and Frank Fritz (later Danielle Colby leading buys) scour barns, attics, and backroads for Americana to resell. Negotiating with collectors and characters across rural towns, they unearth motorcycles, signage, toys, and history, proving one person's rust is another's treasure. Long drives, haggling, and restoration stories make the hunt as engaging as the haul.
data.title: American Pickers

data.description: Luxury charter yacht crew in the Caribbean handle demanding guests, high-sea hazards, and messy boat romances. Captain's orders, galley meltdowns, and tip meetings frame each week as stews and deckhands scramble to deliver white-glove service while living where they work. The original Below Deck spawned a franchise by proving maritime hospitality can be rougher than open water.
data.title: Below Deck

data.description: Engineers and explorers investigate abandoned mega-structures—derelict resorts, Soviet silos, collapsed bridges—using drone footage, CGI recreations, and history to explain why they failed. Each episode pieces together construction ambition, war, economics, or disaster that left concrete giants to crumble, turning modern ruins into case studies on hubris, innovation, and the forces that erase human dreams.
data.title: Mysteries of the Abandoned

data.description: Teams of Canadians dash across provinces and foreign legs, deciphering clues, facing roadblocks, and racing to pit stops. The Amazing Race Canada swaps snowfields for jungles and skyscrapers, celebrating local culture while testing stamina and teamwork. U-turns, alliances, and photo-finish sprints decide who claims the million-dollar prize and national bragging rights each season.
data.title: The Amazing Race Canada

data.description: Karl Pilkington travels the world pondering life's big questions—happiness, death, kids—while reluctantly trying local customs. His deadpan gripes and baffled curiosity contrast with the joy of the people he meets, turning travelogue into a dry, philosophical comedy about how different cultures tackle the same existential headaches.
data.title: The Moaning of Life

data.description: Everybody Loves Raymond creator Phil Rosenthal eats his way through cities from Lisbon to Bangkok, meeting chefs and locals with a dad-joke grin. Each episode blends food porn, cultural curiosity, and video calls home to his parents, making travel and cuisine feel like a global family dinner where humor and generosity are the house specials.
data.title: Somebody Feed Phil

data.description: Philomena Cunk delivers a mockumentary tour of civilization, asking experts absurd questions about pyramids, the Renaissance, and streaming media with a perfectly straight face. Deadpan narration, mismatched stock footage, and running gags about Vivaldi turn history lessons into sharp satire, proving ignorance can be a powerful comedic lens on humanity's biggest achievements.
data.title: Cunk on Earth

data.description: Extreme athletes chase first descents and lines on remote peaks, jungles, and rivers for a four-part HBO doc. Each expedition couples breathtaking drone shots with real risk—avalanches, rapids, storms—while showing the logistics, camaraderie, and environmental stakes of pushing into Earth's last untouched edges.
data.title: Edge of the Earth

data.description: Long Way Home follows veterans and refugees motorbiking across continents to return to places that shaped them. Border hassles, mechanical failures, and roadside hospitality turn each mile into a meditation on displacement, healing, and the roads that connect past and future. Cinematic drone vistas pair with intimate campfire confessions.
data.title: Long Way Home

data.description: House Hunters International drops homebuyers into foreign markets—from Paris studios to Costa Rican eco-lodges—as they weigh location, budget, and lifestyle. Real estate tours reveal cultural quirks and personal priorities, making property hunting a window into how people reimagine home when they cross borders.
data.title: House Hunters International

data.description: In Long Way Up, Ewan McGregor and Charley Boorman ride prototype electric Harleys from Ushuaia to Los Angeles. Ice roads, altitude, and charging gaps test the tech and friendship while a support crew films border crossings and local encounters. The journey doubles as a road movie about sustainable travel and the bond forged over countless miles.
data.title: Long Way Up

data.description: Illusionist David Blaine pushes the limits of endurance and disbelief in one-off feats—helium balloon flights, ice blocks, underwater breath holds—captured in cinematic detail. Do Not Attempt intercuts stunt prep, medical monitoring, and reactions from onlookers, underscoring how curiosity, danger, and spectacle collide when a performer keeps asking how far the human body can go.
data.title: David Blaine: Do Not Attempt

data.description: Chef Andrew Zimmern travels the globe to eat the dishes most travelers fear—fermented shark, insects, offal—discovering culture through flavor and courage. His curiosity and respect for hosts turn shock food into anthropology, revealing how scarcity, tradition, and taste shape what counts as delicious from Minnesota diners to Mongolian steppes.
data.title: Bizarre Foods with Andrew Zimmern

data.description: After lost luggage forces him to dress like a local, Conan experiences Norway with musician Jarle and fish farmer Kai, spars with Vikings, and chases the Northern Lights.
data.title: Norway

data.description: In Buenos Aires, Conan trains with a football club, shares asado with Jordan Schlansky, and learns what it means to be a Gaucho.
data.title: Argentina

data.description: Conan's mental and physical resolve are tested in Bangkok as he faces a Muay Thai fighter, a python, and deep-fried scorpion.
data.title: Thailand

data.description: While chasing his roots in Ireland, Conan tries local speech, sings with The Irish Tenors, and acts on a long-running soap opera.
data.title: Ireland

data.description: In Madrid, Conan picks olives with Jordan Schlansky, flies a simulator, and tours the city with Javier Bardem.
data.title: Spain

data.description: Conan attempts a world record with Taika Waititi and meets podcast fan Riley in his off-grid container home.
data.title: New Zealand

data.description: After delivering a long-overdue Team Coco shirt to a loyal fan, Conan performs with the Vienna Boys' Choir and channels his inner Freud in Austria.
data.title: Austria

data.description: Americans leave home to build lives abroad with partners they've been dating long-distance, navigating visas in reverse. Culture clashes, language gaps, skeptical families, and tight budgets test whether love survives outside the U.S. Comfort zones shrink as couples juggle bureaucracy with weddings, making each season a reminder that romance requires resilience as much as romance.
data.title: 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way

data.description: Each standalone episode of Accused begins with a defendant in court; flashbacks unravel how ordinary choices spiraled into alleged crimes. The anthology tackles hot-button issues—justice bias, online shaming, vigilante impulses—asking viewers to decide guilt before the verdict drops. Its rotating casts and moral gray zones keep every hour a fresh ethical debate.
data.title: Accused

data.description: After xenomorph sightings are dismissed as myth, an investigative team on a rapidly industrializing Earth uncovers biocorp conspiracies, ancient Engineer tech, and a hive hidden beneath a megacity. Survival horror meets hard sci-fi as Weyland-Yutani factions race to weaponize the ultimate organism, forcing unlikely allies to choose between profit, species survival, and their own humanity.
data.title: Alien: Earth

data.description: Through police interviews and court footage, Amanda Knox recounts her Italian murder trial, media frenzy, and years of appeals. Journalists and prosecutors defend their narratives, illustrating how tabloids, cultural bias, and prosecutorial pride can eclipse evidence in the scramble to assign guilt.
data.title: Amanda Knox

data.description: Traveling back in time isn't simple, as James Cole (Bruce Willis) learns the hard way. Imprisoned in the 2030s, James is recruited for a mission that will send him back to the 1990s. Once there, he's supposed to gather information about a nascent plague that's about to exterminate the vast majority of the world's population. But, aside from the manic Jeffrey (Brad Pitt), he gets little in the way of cooperation, not least from medical gatekeepers like Dr. Kathryn Railly (Madeleine Stowe).
data.title: 12 Donkeys

data.description: Ava DuVernay revisits U.S. history from the 13th Amendment to mass incarceration, arguing that a loophole for “punishment for crime” enabled Black Codes, Jim Crow, and the War on Drugs. Scholars, activists, and politicians tie policy to profit, asking whether the carceral state is slavery by another name.
data.title: 13th

data.description: Eyewitnesses and newly released tapes revisit the fall of the Berlin Wall: East German protests, Stasi files burned in basements, and a botched press conference that opened the border. The documentary shows how ordinary citizens, miscommunications, and geopolitical fatigue ended a divided city overnight and reshaped Europe.
data.title: 1989: The Fall of the Berlin Wall

data.description: Filmmaker Damon Gameau visits researchers and farmers to model a future 2040 if today's solutions scale: regenerative agriculture storing carbon, seaweed farms feeding cattle to cut methane, microgrids powering villages, and transport swaps that shrink oil demand. Animated “what if” sequences turn policy whitepapers into hope-filled storyboards.

Cameras follow Kenyan marathoner Eliud Kipchoge's quest to break the two-hour barrier. Wind-tunnel testing of pacing formations, laser-guided splits, and bespoke shoes meet philosophical musings on discipline. The Vienna run shows how precision teamwork and one runner's calm reshaped what humans believe is possible.
data.title: 2:00:00 - Kipchoge's Impossible Run

data.description: Using bottle dives and microplastic trawls, “A Plastic Ocean” shows how discarded packaging breaks into toxic confetti eaten by fish and returned to human plates. Remote atolls piled with debris, seabirds starved by full bellies, and recycling economists reveal both the scale of the problem and circular-economy fixes already working.
data.title: A Plastic Ocean

data.description: A Utah family befriends a charismatic neighbor who kidnaps their daughter twice, manipulating parents and exploiting religious trust. Interviews, FBI testimony, and archived TV appearances reveal how grooming, gaslighting, and community silence let a predator operate in plain sight.
data.title: Abducted in Plain Sight

data.description: America's Test Kitchen methodically reverse-engineers recipes, testing dozens of variations to deliver foolproof results. Blind tastings, equipment reviews, and science explainers turn home cooking into approachable R&D, empowering viewers with techniques rather than trends across hundreds of half-hour episodes filmed in an ever-busier Boston kitchen.
data.title: America's Test Kitchen

data.description: After three years in prison for killing neo-Nazis who attacked his family, Derek Vinyard tries to pull his younger brother Danny away from the white-supremacist gang he once led. Flashbacks reveal how rage and propaganda radicalized him, while the present forces Derek to confront old allies, mend shattered family trust, and decide whether redemption can overpower the cycle of hate he set in motion.
data.title: American History X

data.description: When a Colorado mother and her two daughters vanish, police bodycams, neighbor videos, and text messages unravel the facade of a perfect family. Investigators chart Chris Watts' shifting stories until forensic evidence and failed polygraphs force a confession, exposing the banality and brutality of familicide in suburbia.
data.title: American Murder: The Family Next Door

data.description: Pickers Mike Wolfe and Frank Fritz (later Danielle Colby leading buys) scour barns, attics, and backroads for Americana to resell. Negotiating with collectors and characters across rural towns, they unearth motorcycles, signage, toys, and history, proving one person's rust is another's treasure. Long drives, haggling, and restoration stories make the hunt as engaging as the haul.
data.title: American Pickers

data.description: Archaeologists and radar scans peel back layers of Angkor Wat, revealing hydraulic canals, hidden shrines, and why the Khmer Empire collapsed. Monsoon failures, political strife, and shifting trade routes are mapped across jungle temples, linking past resilience to present-day preservation battles in Cambodia.
data.title: Angkor Wat: Secrets of the Empire

data.description: Class 3-E must assassinate their homeroom teacher—a tentacled superbeing who plans to destroy Earth after graduation—while he teaches them study habits and self-worth. Assassination Classroom balances slapstick training with heartfelt growth as misfit students discover talent under impossible pressure, turning a wild premise into a surprisingly sincere tale of mentorship and second chances.
data.title: Ansatsu Kyoushitsu (Assassination Classroom)

data.description: Chef and author Anthony Bourdain travels from Beirut to Brooklyn night markets, eating with locals, cooks, and taxi drivers to reveal politics, history, and humor through food. The show's handheld style, punk soundtrack, and frank narration made it less a travel brochure than a culinary anthropology class, inspiring viewers to chase flavor over fine dining and empathy over clichés.
data.title: Anthony Bourdain: No Reservations

data.description: Anthony Bourdain roams 80 cities on Parts Unknown, eating in markets, war zones, and family kitchens to map culture through flavor. The series mixes handheld meals, jazz scores, and candid politics, showing how food reveals memory, conflict, and resilience—whether at a Hanoi bun cha stall or a West Virginia diner shuttered by opioid grief.
data.title: Anthony Bourdain: Parts Unknown

data.description: “Arctic Tale” follows a polar bear cub and a walrus calf growing up on shrinking sea ice. Hunting lessons, playful slides, and first swims are shadowed by thinning floes and longer swims to food. Narration links their intimate struggles to the broader story of a warming Arctic reshaping cultures and food webs.
data.title: Arctic Tale

data.description: In Buenos Aires, Conan trains with a football club, shares asado with Jordan Schlansky, and learns what it means to be a Gaucho.
data.title: Argentina

data.description: Through letters, cockpit audio, and family interviews, the film follows Neil Armstrong from Navy test flights to commanding Apollo 11. Simulations, fatal training accidents, and the moon EVA reveal a stoic engineer balancing grief and fame, while post-mission years show his retreat to teaching and quiet advocacy for space safety.
data.title: Armstrong

data.description: Sixties superspy Austin Powers is thawed in the 1990s to stop bald archvillain Dr. Evil from holding the world ransom. Armed with crushed-velvet suits, dubious dental work, and unlimited “mojo,” Austin fumbles through culture shock, seduction, and spycraft alongside agent Vanessa Kensington, proving that shagadelic confidence sometimes beats high-tech espionage when global catastrophe is on the line.
data.title: Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery

data.description: After delivering a long-overdue Team Coco shirt to a loyal fan, Conan performs with the Vienna Boys' Choir and channels his inner Freud in Austria.
data.title: Austria

data.description: Orphan Xiao Yan loses his powers, then gains a mentor and a mystical ring that kickstart his climb through the Dou Qi ranks. Facing clan intrigue, alchemists, and demonic beasts, he tempers talent with hard-forged discipline. The Chinese 3D donghua adapts the xianxia novel into sweeping cultivation battles and romance across multiple seasons of fiery duels and pill refining.
data.title: Battle Through the Heavens

data.description: Chefs try to dethrone Iron Chef champ Bobby Flay in a two-round sprint: first beating a peer to earn the right to challenge him, then facing Bobby on a surprise signature ingredient. Blind tastings decide if the upstart's dish can outshine Flay's mastery, making each episode a compact culinary duel of speed, strategy, and swagger.
data.title: Beat Bobby Flay

data.description: Leonardo DiCaprio travels from sinking Pacific atolls to Alberta's tar sands, grilling ministers, oil CEOs, and climate scientists. Animated carbon budget charts and Papal interviews push viewers to weigh policy, diet, and energy choices, arguing that denial is no longer a political option as feedback loops accelerate.
data.title: Before the Flood

data.description: Luxury charter yacht crew in the Caribbean handle demanding guests, high-sea hazards, and messy boat romances. Captain's orders, galley meltdowns, and tip meetings frame each week as stews and deckhands scramble to deliver white-glove service while living where they work. The original Below Deck spawned a franchise by proving maritime hospitality can be rougher than open water.
data.title: Below Deck

data.description: Guts the Black Swordsman swings an iron slab of a blade across a world of apostles, demonic eclipses, and corrupt kings. Haunted by the Band of the Hawk's betrayal, he travels with witch Schierke and cursed lover Casca, battling fate itself. The dark fantasy fuses brutal combat with meditations on trauma and free will, continuing a legendary manga's bleak, operatic saga.
data.title: Berserk

data.description: Best Medicine is a dramedy about a failing rural clinic that crowdsources innovation—3D-printed casts, telehealth, barter economies—to keep doors open. A burnt-out doc, a hacker nurse, and a newly minted PA juggle quirky patients and bureaucratic hurdles, proving that improvisation and community can be lifesaving tools when budgets and bandwidth run dry.
data.title: Best Medicine

data.description: Surfing prodigy Bethany Hamilton loses an arm to a shark at 13, then fights back to world tour form. Training montages, adaptive board rigs, and wipeouts show resilience; interviews explore faith, motherhood, and what it means to redefine strength when the ocean that injured you remains your greatest pull.
data.title: Bethany Hamilton: Unstoppable

data.description: Ex-con lawyer Jimmy McGill slowly transforms into Saul Goodman, “criminal” attorney for the underworld. From elder-law scams to cartel money laundering, the prequel traces brotherly betrayal, love for Kim Wexler, and moral erosion. Meticulous visuals, desert cons, and courtroom feints show how the pursuit of success can warp talent into tragedy.
data.title: Better Call Saul

data.description: Chef Andrew Zimmern travels the globe to eat the dishes most travelers fear—fermented shark, insects, offal—discovering culture through flavor and courage. His curiosity and respect for hosts turn shock food into anthropology, revealing how scarcity, tradition, and taste shape what counts as delicious from Minnesota diners to Mongolian steppes.
data.title: Bizarre Foods with Andrew Zimmern

data.description: Black photographers, filmmakers, and musicians dissect how images of Blackness are framed, feared, or fetishized. From civil-rights newsreels to Instagram, they examine who holds the camera and why representation still shapes safety, opportunity, and self-definition in America.
data.title: Black Lens

data.description: Anthology of techno-paranoia where each standalone episode imagines near-future worlds warped by screens, AI, social scores, or virtual immortality. Season 7 (2025) brought the total to 33 tales, including the first sequel “USS Callister: Into Infinity.” Dark satire, horror, and bleak humor expose how human frailties, not gadgets, make our black mirrors reflect the worst—and sometimes the best—of us.
data.title: Black Mirror

data.description: A superyacht's crew serves charter guests on the Med, juggling fine dining, tight quarters, and romantic entanglements while captains enforce maritime order. Each charter brings demanding clients, water-toy mishaps, and galley meltdowns, turning every turnaround day into a race against the clock. Seasons hop ports from Croatia to Malta, making luxury hospitality and nautical drama crash together below deck.
data.title: Below Deck Mediterranean

data.description: Former U.S. Vice President Al Gore travels city to city with a slide deck that turns melting glaciers, hurricane tracks, and CO₂ graphs into an urgent plea. Classroom anecdotes mix with bipartisan policy nudges, framing climate change not as distant science but as a solvable civic crisis if voters, businesses, and governments act in time.
data.title: An Inconvenient Truth

data.description: Filmed with lightweight 4K rigs, this sequel returns to frozen seas, coral reefs, and jungles to show behaviors never captured before: mobula rays leaping by moonlight, glass frogs guarding eggs, lizards surfing ocean currents. Each vignette pairs wonder with a quiet warning about bleaching reefs, plastic debris, and the narrow margins animals now navigate.
data.title: Blue Planet II

data.description: Burger slinger Bob Belcher, wife Linda, and kids Tina, Gene, and Louise scrape by running a seaside diner where landlord disputes, health inspections, and talent shows become musical, pun-laden adventures. With heartfelt chaos and running gags, the long-running animated sitcom has reached its 300th episode while keeping the Belchers' optimism, sibling scheming, and burger-of-the-day jokes sizzling.
data.title: Bob's Burgers

data.description: Bon Appétit's test kitchen team—editors, chefs, and food nerds—experiment on camera, perfecting recipes while revealing the flops, science, and jokes in between. From gourmet candy re-creations to weeknight pasta drills, the series made process as addictive as results, inspiring home cooks to chase technique, not just trends.
data.title: Bon Appétit

data.description: When FBI anthropologist Dr. Temperance “Bones” Brennan teams with war veteran Agent Seeley Booth, skeletal remains become stories that reveal killers. Each case mixes forensic science, pop-culture quips, and slow-burn romance, while Brennan's rational worldview clashes with Booth's gut instinct. Over twelve seasons, the Jeffersonian team proves bones rarely lie, but people often do.
data.title: Bones

data.description: Tony Hawk narrates how backyard ramps birthed modern skateboarding. Archival VHS, X Games runs, and hospital bills chart pioneers like Rodney Mullen and Elissa Steamer pushing physics and gender norms. Industry insiders dissect sponsorship booms, video games, and how aging skaters manage bodies built on risk.
data.title: Bones and Boards: A Skate Story

data.description: Tennis legends Borg and McEnroe relive their 1980 Wimbledon clash: icy baseline patience versus fiery serve-and-volley aggression. Match stats, wood-racket physics, and sports psychologists unpack how rivalry forged respect and raised the sport's mental bar.
data.title: Borg vs. McEnroe: Fire and Ice

data.description: At Crane, Poole & Schmidt, eccentric superstar attorneys Alan Shore and Denny Crane win impossible cases with wit, bombast, and occasional mad-cow digressions. Courtroom fireworks tackle tobacco, biotech, and civil liberties, while balcony cigars frame a friendship both absurd and profound. Boston Legal mixes sharp legal issues with outrageous comedy and sudden pathos.
data.title: Boston Legal

data.description: Struggling chemistry teacher Walter White turns to cooking meth after a cancer diagnosis, dragging former student Jesse Pinkman into a criminal empire. As the blue product spreads, lies, violence, and ego transform Walt from family man into Heisenberg, shattering everyone in his orbit. Five seasons of meticulous plotting made this a landmark of tension, morality, and antihero storytelling.
data.title: Breaking Bad

data.description: Narrated by David Attenborough and scientist Johan Rockström, this film visualizes the nine planetary boundaries—climate, biodiversity, oceans, freshwater—and shows how collapsing ice shelves, burning forests, and bleaching reefs signal tipping points. Hopeful case studies outline how rapid policy shifts could stabilize Earth's life-support systems still within reach.
data.title: Breaking Boundaries: The Science of Our Planet
Breaking Up is Hard to Do

data.description: Brilliant Minds (formerly Dr. Wolfe) centers on a revolutionary neurologist and her elite team treating rare brain disorders with cutting-edge tech and audacious surgeries. As they decode consciousness and identity, office politics, FDA battles, and patient consent test how far genius should push. The series mixes medical puzzles with ethical landmines and a dash of workplace romance.
data.title: Brilliant Minds

data.description: In 1950s East London, midwives at Nonnatus House bicycle through cobbled streets delivering babies, confronting poverty, racism, and evolving medical norms. Orders of nuns work alongside secular nurses as the NHS is born, blending gentle period detail with social-issue storytelling. Annual Christmas specials and ongoing seasons keep the drama intimate, hopeful, and grounded in community care.
data.title: Call the Midwife

data.description: NASA, ESA, and NOAA scientists race to decode why coral reefs are bleaching at record rates. Underwater macro shots show symbiotic algae abandoning corals; drone surveys map reefs turning ghostly white. Local fishers, Pacific islanders, and marine biologists weigh what losing reefs means for food, storms, and culture.
data.title: Chasing Coral

data.description: Photographer James Balog deploys time-lapse cameras on Greenland, Alaska, and Iceland ice fronts to witness glaciers racing backward. Shattering seracs, collapsing melt ponds, and multi-year sequences become visual proof of warming, while field teams battle broken tripods, frostbite, and crevasse fields to keep the record rolling.
data.title: Chasing Ice

data.description: Chef's Table serves cinematic portraits of world-class chefs—from Modena to Bangkok—lingering on smoke, sauce, and philosophy. Each episode pairs slow-motion kitchens with the personal histories, failures, and obsessions behind a signature dish, redefining food TV as arthouse biography where flavor, memory, and culture share the same plate.
data.title: Chef's Table

data.description: Through declassified memos and survivor testimony, this film reconstructs the 1986 Chernobyl meltdown: control-room errors, delayed evacuations, and the heroism of firefighters and divers who stemmed radioactive lava. It examines Soviet secrecy, the Exclusion Zone's lasting scars, and how nuclear policy shifted worldwide after the plume crossed continents.
data.title: Chernobyl: Inside the Disaster

data.description: Chicago Med follows the city's newest state-of-the-art trauma center, where Dr. Will Halstead, Dr. Ethan Choi, and colleagues juggle mass-casualty codes, gang-violence wounds, and tangled romances. Linked to the One Chicago universe, cases often cross with police and fire crews, showing how frontline teams coordinate under relentless pressure and dwindling resources.
data.title: Chicago Med

data.description: Set against Shanghai's neon boom, this documentary examines how modern China was carved by Opium Wars, civil strife, Japanese invasion, and Communist revolution. Economists and historians track how treaty ports, railways, and state planning forged today's superpower while leaving contested memories in textbooks and public squares.
data.title: China: A Century of Revolution

data.description: Edward Snowden's life after the Hong Kong hotel: asylum in Moscow, encrypted calls with journalists, and his marriage lived under surveillance risk. Philosophers and cryptographers debate whistleblowing ethics while Snowden codes privacy tools, insisting that ordinary citizens deserve agency over their data.
data.title: Citizen Snowden

data.description: Journalist Glenn Greenwald, filmmaker Laura Poitras, and NSA contractor Edward Snowden meet in a Hong Kong hotel to expose mass surveillance. Claustrophobic room scenes, encrypted uploads, and global headlines show how secrecy gives way to the most consequential leak of the digital age—and its personal cost for the leaker.
data.title: Citizenfour
